The decision has made after “apocalyptic” wildfires broke out across the West Midlands and parts of the rest of the UK yesterday – as a result of the heatwave.

News.title: Two prisoners charged after Sara Sharif’s killer dad ‘has neck & face sliced open with tuna tin lid in jail cell’
News.content:
JAIL HORROR Two prisoners charged after Sara Sharif’s killer dad ‘has neck & face sliced open with tuna tin lid in jail cell’

TWO prisoners have been charged after Sara Sharif’s dad had his neck and face slashed open with a tuna tin lid in his jail cell.

Urfan Sharif, 43, was allegedly ambushed in his cell at HMP Belmarsh, South London, last year.



It came just weeks into his life sentence for murdering ten-year-old Sara after a sickening campaign of abuse.

The Crown Prosecution Service today confirmed Steven Sansom and Adam Watson have been charged with attempted murder and section 18 offences.



Samson, 47 and Watson, 39, will appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on August 26.

Daren Streeter, Deputy Chief Crown Prosecutor in CPS London, said:

“The Crown Prosecution Service has decided to charge Steven Sansom and Adam Watson with attempted murder in connection to an incident at HMP Belmarsh in January 2025.

“Our prosecutors have worked closely with the Metropolitan Police to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring the case to court and pursue criminal proceedings.

“We remind all concerned that proceedings against the defendants are active and they have the right to a fair trial. It is vital that there should be no reporting, commentary or sharing of information which could in anyway prejudice these proceedings.”

The Sun revealed how Sharif was lucky to survive the jail attack last January.



A source said at the time: “He was sliced in the neck and face, and is still in healthcare and in a very bad way.

“He was lucky to survive, has had to have stitches and will have scars as a permanent reminder of the attack.

“Something like this was always on the cards, and an attack was probably only a matter of time.”



Tragic Sara was hooded, burned and bitten by Urfan Sharif and her stepmum Beinash Batool as they dished out sadistic “punishments”.

She was found bludgeoned to death with at least 71 internal injuries at home in Woking, Surrey, on August 10 last year.

Sharif, 42, his wife Batool, 30, and brother Faisal Malik, 29, were at the centre of a global manhunt after fleeing the UK after her death.

Once he landed in Pakistan, the evil dad called police to confess his daughter was dead after he beat her up “too much”.

Sharif wept as he and Batool were jailed for life with a minimum of 40 years and 33 years after being convicted of murder.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sara’s uncle Malik was also jailed for 16 years after being cleared of murder but found guilty of causing or allowing her death.

It later emerged authorities missed at least 15 opportunities to save Sara before her brutal death.

News.title: Brit schoolgirl, 12, missing in Japan after vanishing on family holiday as cops scour CCTV showing her last sighting
News.content:
DESPERATE SEARCH Brit schoolgirl, 12, missing in Japan after vanishing on family holiday as cops scour CCTV showing her last sighting

A 12-YEAR-OLD British girl has been reported missing in Japan after vanishing on her family holiday, sparking a frantic search operation.

Carmelita Lakdesha Paul arrived in Japan for sightseeing with her parents and older brother on July 21.



Her family said they last saw her on August 12, at their Tokyo apartment but when they woke up the next morning she was gone.

Carmelita’s father had spoken with her just the night before and said there was nothing suspicious about his daughters behaviour.



Police received a missing persons report from the family at 9.30am on August 13.

Carmelita’s phone was still in the private rental, so the family had no way of contacting their missing daughter.

CCTV footage analysed by cops shows the 12-year-old dressed in a blue sleeveless top, black and white skirt, black pumps and carrying a pink handbag.

She was seen walking in the Nichome section of Kamata, near to where the family were staying, later that morning.

Investigators said she then boarded a train at Kamata station and travelled 20 minutes south to Yokohama Station.

But cops have not been able to trace her movements any further from this point.



Carmelita – described as being 5ft 3in and a medium build with curly black hair – did not take her passport with her when she left the property.

And her family believes she had only a few thousand yen (less than £70) on her.

The small sum would not be enough for an extended stay at a hotel or hostel – heightening the families fears of her safety.

Japan has also been battered by severe rainstorms making proper shelter even more important.

At least eight people have died after record breaking rainfall triggered horror flooding, landslides, power cuts and transport chaos across the countries east.



Residents and tourists fled the devastation, with nearly 7,000 people stranded at Tokyo’s Narita airport on Thursday.

Chiba, near Tokyo, has logged more than 100mm (3.9in) of rain per hour since Thursday afternoon – the highest volume ever recorded in the country.

Authorities are urging anyone with information that could help find Carmelita to contact Tokyo Metropolitan Police’s Kamata Station.

The Sun has approached the UK foreign office for comment.

News.title: Two-year-old airlifted to hospital with serious injuries after being hit by an electric bike
News.content:
TOT HORROR Two-year-old airlifted to hospital with serious injuries after being hit by an electric bike

A TODDLER has been airlifted to hospital with serious injuries after being hit by a bike.

The two-year-old was rushed to hospital yesterday at around 9pm in Clacton.

Cops raced to the scene but the rider failed to stop at the scene.

They have been described as wearing a grey hoodie top and a balaclava.





The electric bike involved in the collision is described as having a scrambler design with red handlebars.

Several witnesses were stopped at the scene and now police are pursuing several lines of enquiry and appealing for information from the public.

Tendring District Commander Chief Inspector Stuart Austin said: “I understand the local community will be extremely concerned following this incident.

“We know the dangerous and anti-social use of e-bikes, e-scooters and motorcycles impacts residents across town. We are committed to tackling the issue.



“During a two-day operation at the end of last month we seized 27 vehicles and e-scooters. This work will continue.

“Officers from our Neighbourhood Policing Team are working alongside specialist roads policing officers to target those who ignore the law and put others at risk.

“A child has been hurt, and we are working at pace to locate the person responsible. I would urge anyone who can help to get in touch.”

Police have said that any information, CCTV, dash cam or other footage relating to this incident, should be sent to the force, quoting 1436 of 13 August.



If you would like to make an anonymous report you can contact independent charity Crimestoppers, by visiting their website or by calling 0800 555 111.

News.title: Heartless mum left her six dogs to starve to death in squalid home surrounded by faeces – but avoids jail
News.content:
DOG TRAGEDY Heartless mum left her six dogs to starve to death in squalid home surrounded by faeces – but avoids jail

A HEARTLESS mum who left six dogs to starve to death in their own filth has avoided jail.

Victoria Fowles left the chihuahua-type dogs to fend for themselves when she moved out of her former home in Lowestoft, Suffolk.



An estate manager who visited the house found it in an “atrocious condition with dog mess throughout the ground floor and an awful smell”.

The manager discovered three of the tragic dogs in a basket in the rear dining room of the property.



RSPCA inspector Ben Kirby later attended with the manager and found the bodies of the dogs in the basket had been moved.

When they checked the shed in the back garden, they found them in a bag along with three more decomposed bodies.

Fowles admitted causing unnecessary suffering to her dogs at an earlier hearing, and offence under the Animal Welfare Act 2006.

The charge stated that she had failed to provide proper and necessary care and supervision to protect them between February 10, 2025, and April 4 last year.



Fowles avoided a jail term and was instead handed a 12 month sentence, suspended for two years.

She was also disqualified from keeping all animals for life, or until further order, and ordered to pay costs of £300, and a victim surcharge of £187.

Great Yarmouth Magistrates’ Court was told Inspector Kirby contacted Suffolk Police in order to seize the bodies of the dogs for evidence purposes.

An expert vet said in their report the dogs were found in various stages of decomposition, and all were estimated to have a body condition score of just one out of nine.

The vet concluded that lack of food and water significantly contributed to the dogs’ suffering – leading to their death.



Their suffering included starvation and dehydration, psychological distress, deprivation of human companionship and overgrown nails.

They were left in agony for a minimum of several weeks over “a protracted period of time”, it was said.

Inspector Kirby of the RSPCA said after the case: “It is heartbreaking to think that these poor dogs were just abandoned and left to suffer what would have been a harrowing death and that their deaths were completely unnecessary and avoidable.”

News.title: Shock pics show killer whale blasted by shotgun in Strait of Gibraltar after spate of terrifying orca attacks on boats
News.content:
A RARE “Grandmother” killer whale appears to have been blasted with a shotgun in the Strait of Gibraltar.

A shocking photo shows the Iberian orca known as Toñi as she was found with eight suspected gunshot wounds on her dorsal fin.



It comes after a terrifying spate of attacks by the animals on boats in the area, with five clashes in just 48 hours in July.

Toñi is the oldest known killer whale in her pack and is known as “la Abuela” – “the Grandmother” in English.



Whale watcher Paco Gil shared a photo showing the holes on the endangered animal.

The concerning wounds appeared suddenly on the matriarch on August 12, leading conservationists to suspect a violent attack on the orca.

Conservation group Orca Iberica said the injuries were likely caused by a “shotgun blast”.

The group said the predator was likely fired on with a gun normally used for hunting wild boars.

They wrote on Facebook: “Toñi arrived at the Strait with marks consistent with ulcerations caused by a shotgun blast, possibly from 9mm diameter lead shot intended for wild boar.

“Each cartridge contains nine pellets in three layers (buckshot), which are the marks on the fin.



“This type of ammunition is fired from a 12/70 gauge shotgun at a distance of less than 15 meters, as it spreads 25 cm every 10 meters.”

Orcas are legally protected in Spain, listing Toñi’s population who swim around the Strait of Gibraltar and the Gulf of Cádiz as endangered.

Pursuing, killing, capturing or disturbing the animals is illegal.

It comes as incidents of orcas attacking boats have increased in recent years.

The huge animals have been spotted making contact with rudders, in some cases causing serious damage.



In 2022, an orca called Gladis was thought to be teaching gangs to attack yachts, sinking at least three boats.

But Spanish authorities and scientists have repeatedly said that these clashes are not attacks.

Instead, orca specialists say the interactions are the animals playing with the ships, rather than acts of aggression.

The suspected killer whale shooting has been reported to the Spanish authorities.

Whale watcher Janek Andre told The Telegraph that the injured orca was found between Tarifa in Spain and Tangiers in Morocco in the Strait of Gibraltar.



He said: “We recognise it is the same orca as we have been studying their dorsals for three years.

“We noticed what looked like shotgun pellet wounds and checked this with people in the ministry who know about shotguns, [and they] said it looked like pellet wounds.”

Andre added: “It is another dimension of human aggression towards the orca. Who the hell would shoot a critically endangered species?”

News.title: Met Office map shows MASSIVE band of rain soaking UK next week just hours after hottest day of the year
News.content:
A MASSIVE band of rain is set to soak the UK next week, only hours after Brits basked in the hottest day of the year.

The relief from the prolonged dry weather comes as nearly three-quarters of England and the entirety of Wales faces drought.

Rain is set to return to Britain from Monday evening into the early hours of Tuesday morning after weeks of high temperatures.



Yesterday, Britain recorded its hottest day of the year, with staggering 38.1C temperatures reached in Kew Gardens, West London.



This came as part of the fifth heatwave of the year, which saw extreme heat amber health alerts declared across large swathes of the country.

However, the Met Office has forecast an incoming change to the dry conditions, with a band of rain making its way across the country next week.

From Monday evening next week into Tuesday, there could be rain pushing into northern England and north Wales, with a chance it will descend further into the south of England.



By around 10am on Tuesday, the weather is expected to have mostly cleared from across England, moving eastwards into Europe.

This chance of rainfall comes as nearly three-quarters of England and all of Wales face drought status as a result of consistently dry conditions.



According to the National Drought Group, England faced its driest July since records began 190 years ago, with parts of Hampshire, the Isle of Wight and West Sussex not experiencing rain for over two months.

Over 1,000 wildfires were recorded across England and Wales in July and August, according to data shared by the National Fire Chiefs Council, as Prime Minister Andy Burnham pushes to ban disposable BBQs.

In response to the drought and the dry conditions, over 27million Brits currently face hosepipe ban restrictions, which have been enforced by nine water companies to prevent unnecessary water use.

No water company has confirmed when the restrictions will end, but it is anticipated for when water levels are replenished.

Over the weekend, Northern Ireland, Scotland and potentially eastern England may also be hit by thunderstorms and heavy downpours, with a few showers expected for northern Scotland.

News.title: Builders find hidden gold haul worth an eye-watering sum while renovating cellar… and admit they were tempted to KEEP it
News.content:
FINDERS KEEPERS Builders find hidden gold haul worth an eye-watering sum while renovating cellar… and admit they were tempted to KEEP it

STUNNED builders stumbled upon a hidden £7.5million gold haul stashed inside the walls of a cellar – and admitted they were very tempted to keep it.

A trove of gold coins and ingots were found bricked into a cellar wall at a former brewery the crew were renovating in northern Belgium.



The building crew had been carrying out run-of-the-mill groundworks to lay a pipe for the sewer system before the eye-watering discovery.

Kobe, an 18-year-old working on the site, told VRT news: “At first I thought they were €1 coins.



“Our first reaction was actually disbelief, amazement. We certainly hadn’t expected to find gold.”

When they removed sections of the foundations, the builders quickly realised the mountain of gold they had discovered.

Site manager Mario said: “They shouted: ‘We’ve found gold!’ I went to have a look and picked up the gold.

“We kept digging up more coins and bars. Only then did it really sink in what we’d found. It was a strange feeling.”

Asked whether they’d considered keeping the stash for themselves, Mario said: “There are so many coins and bars; it would be almost impossible.

“Besides, that would be theft.”



Kobe said: “Of course, we did briefly consider keeping it. But it’s simply too much money.

“If it were a few thousand euros, it might be feasible. But €9million (£7.5m) – you simply can’t keep that hidden.

The crew quickly notified police and their client, a charity called CAW Oost-Vlaanderen, about the find.



Cops have launched a probe into how the treasure ended up in the building.

Many of the gold bars are reportedly stamped around 1957 to 1961.

Geert Hillaert, director of CAW Oost-Vlaanderen, said police would have to establish whether the hoard was linked to criminal activity.

He added that it may take many years to locate the true owners.

Geert said: “For all we know, this discovery is the result of some kind of fraudulent activity and the gold has been hidden there.”



If the gold does eventually go to the charity, Geert said it would be “a very welcome gift” to help the “enormous need” they face every day.

He said: “We will create additional capacity for our target group across the whole of East Flanders,” referring to the homeless.

Kobe said that he hopes there might be a finder’s fee for him and his colleagues.

Mario said: “After 33 years in the construction industry, this is the first time I’ve experienced anything like this.

“I don’t think it will ever happen again.”



Gold hunters have meanwhile been warned to “stay away” from the building by police.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cop Patrick Feys said: “After the treasure was found, the whole site was turned upside down. We’re certain there’s nothing left to find.”

He warned that, as the building was being demolished, it would be dangerous for people to crowd around the site.

News.title: Meghan Markle shares sweet pregnancy advice to expectant singer at star-studded gala
News.content:
Meghan Markle shares sweet pregnancy advice to expectant singer at star-studded gala

The Duchess of Sussex attended a charity event where she met pregnant singer Pia Toscano and she shared a wholesome interaction with her after her performance.

View 5 Images Meghan and Harry attended the charity gala in Canada last weekend (Image: Jonathan Brady/PA Wire)

Meghan Markle shared a sweet moment with a pregnant singer at a glitzy charity event, offering the soon-to-be mother some advice. It came as the Duke and Duchess of Sussex attended a charity gala for the David Foster Foundation in Canada, when they dressed to the nines for the star-studded event.

‌



At the event, pregnant singer Pia Toscano spoke to Meghan, after she performed the song Feeling Good in front of the crowd. Following her rousing performance, Pia approached Harry and Meghan, who were seated at the head table, when the Duchess spoke to her about her pregnancy and offered her congratulations.

‌

Meghan has spoken proudly about being a mum to Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, in many previous interviews, most recently saying how she views motherhood as a ‘superpower’, adding how her daughter inspires her to be brave when she is having moments of self-doubt.

Meghan made the comments while answering questions from youngsters to promote Cookie Queens, the latest documentary from her and Prince Harry's production company, Archewell Productions. In a Q&A video with InStyle, Meghan was asked by one child what she believed her superpower to be.

News.title: Donald Trump orders changes to aircraft carriers to use steam catapults to launch jets
News.content:
Donald Trump orders changes to aircraft carriers to use steam catapults to launch jets

US President Donald Trump has issued a controversial order to revert aircraft carrier technology to an old steam take-off method, a refit which will cost the US military billions of dollars

View 3 Images The US president wants to go back to an old method of launching jets like this F/A -18E Super Hornet from carriers (Image: US NAVY/NAVCENT PUBLIC AFFAIRS/AFP via Getty Images)

US President Donald Trump has ordered a multi-billion pound ditching of new and high-tech aircraft carrier launching systems for the traditional steam-driven catapult and take-off ramps.

‌



He has also told Navy and Pentagon chiefs to replace USS Ford’s electromagnetic weapons systems with a different system of lifting weaponry. Trump has long complained about the digital system that governs how America’s modern-day fast jets take to the air off US aircraft carriers.

‌



And the switch-back to the old system is likely to cost many billions at a period when the war in Iran is depleting America’s weapons and missiles. The old system of launching will also mean more sailors have to become involved in the less-automated process of taking off during combat missions. Under the more modern system currently in use - the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System - many experts believe it launches planes at faster speeds.

‌



View 3 Images Trump's decision will cost billions of dollars (Image: AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein)

Ukraine's desperate appeal for US Patriot defence missiles before winter arrives READ MORE :

It is also believed to be easier to maintain at sea, takes up far less space on the vessel and the Trump changes come at a time when the US Navy is short of sailors. At the start of the year, the US Navy had about 20,000 unfilled posts across the fleet. In February, the Navy touted the modern take-off system in a press release that said it allowed the USS Ford to launch and recover aircraft at a higher rate than its predecessor, the Nimitz-class ships.

‌



His directive orders the fourth Ford-class carrier, the USS Doris Miller, to be the first ship to include the new changes. That will leave the USS Gerald R. Ford, which is currently in the Middle East, untouched. Trump’s discomfort with the new technology goes back to at least 2017 in his first term.

View 3 Images British jets like these F-35B Lightning jets use different technology for take-offs (Image: LPhot Helayna Birkett/Royal Navy / SWNS)

Then he said the new system is “not good” and “doesn’t have the power” of the older, steam systems in an interview with Time magazine. He said: “You’re going to goddamned steam.” And he has repeated his obsession with old carrier technology on many occasions. As Trump tries to turn back the latest technology, China’s new aircraft carriers employ electromagnetic catapults, and France plans to use the system on its new carrier.

Article continues below

Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said recently that the cost of the Iran war cost grew to £28 billion so far but it is possible it has cost much more. British jets take off from £3.5bn Royal Navy aircraft carriers HMS Queen Elizabeth and HMS Prince of Wales using a ski-ramp at the bow of the ship. This is instead of using steam or electromagnetic catapults and is called the Short Take-Off and Vertical Landing variant specifically for the F-35B Lightning II fighter.

But this decision was controversial since the vertical landing mechanism and manoeuvring involved uses up lots of fuel , significantly reducing the range of the plane on operations.

News.title: Man arrested after 'attempted abduction' of girl under 10 from street in Barrow
News.content:
Man arrested after 'attempted abduction' of girl under 10 from street in Barrow

A man has been arrested following an alleged attempted abduction of a girl aged under 10 in Rawlinson Street, Barrow, with police appealing to the public for information

View Image The incident took place in Rawlinson Street (stock image) (Image: Google Maps)

A man has been arrested over an alleged attempted abduction after a young girl was approached in the street.

Police were called to reports that a girl under 10 had been approached by a man in Rawlinson Street, Barrow, at around 7.45pm on Wednesday.

A man was arrested by Cumbria Police over the incident. The force said he has now been released on bail while enquiries continue.

It is understood that no physical contact was made with the child, but the force reiterated that it takes such reports seriously.

Door to door enquiries have been carried out and patrols have increased in the area.

Police warned locals to be vigilant, but at the same time they have urged against unhelpful online speculation and asked for "time to carry out their work and establish the factual circumstances".

An appeal has been made for anyone with information about the case to get in touch, including people who may have CCTV or doorbell footage.

The force said: "A man arrested following an incident in Rawlinson Street in Barrow yesterday evening (12 Aug) has been released on bail whilst police continue with their enquiries.

Article continues below

"As investigations continue, officers are urging anyone with information which may assist to come forward, whilst continuing to encourage people to refrain from online speculation whilst police officers continue their work to establish the circumstances of what has occurred.

"Anyone with information which may assist this investigation is asked to contact police referencing incident 264 of 12 August 2026. People can report online at www.cumbria.police.uk/report-it quoting the incident number, or phone 101."

News.title: 'Mr Whippy-sellers heave a sigh of relief as Binface loses in Clacton'
News.content:
On polling day, at the literally-named ‘Ice Cream and Chips’ kiosk on Clacton Pier, 20-year-old Maddison Dunston was counting the cost of a 99 flake.

“A box of flakes is £40, Whippy mix is £5 a bottle,” she said, countering one of Count Binface’s key political policies – to make 99 Flakes cost 99p. “We just can’t do whippy-with-a-flake any cheaper than £3.” This morning, Mr Whippy-sellers at every price point can heave a sigh of relief. Adele remains privatised. No water bosses will be forced to take a dip in British rivers, people using speakerphone on public transport will escape conscription – and 99p flakes still cost £3 and upwards on the award-winning pier.

As 19-year-old Binface voter Max told us outside Boots this morning, tongue firmly in his cheek, “I’m disappointed. I’d like to have seen Adele nationalised, but I wasn’t sure about banning loud snacks in cinemas.” Count Binface leaves the Sunshine Coast defeated and presumably by starship, but the question left hanging this morning in the Essex heatwave, was whether he has delivered Nigel Farage one of those Shakespearian blows that looks like a scratch but turns out to be fatal.

"I am damned if I am going to stand on a stage, having won a resounding victory... and be demeaned and humiliated by nobodies,” Mr Farage said last night, refusing to attend the official count at a local leisure centre, and instead appearing by video link from “Farage Fest”, an angry Glastonbury on a nearby airfield.

‌



View 6 Images Max, 19, is a Binface voter (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

Anyone squinting into the North Sea off the famous Pier this morning can see that ship has already sailed. Yes, the Reform leader has been overwhelmingly re-elected in his heartland constituency. It’s also true that one in four voters voted for a bin - the biggest vote ever for a novelty candidate.

And today, the parliamentary investigation into the alleged sleaze swirling around Mr Farage’s financial affairs resumes. The Reform leader is currently being investigated over claims he broke parliamentary rules by not declaring £5 million he received from Christopher Harborne or financial help he received from “Posh” George Cottrell.

There had been plenty of swagger from the Reform canvassers in Farage football shirts gathering on the terrace of the beach-facing Wetherspoons on polling day – and there was plenty on the morning after the result. Dionne Marsh, 68, and her husband Tom 73, told us the right man won. “It’s absolutely ridiculous, 9,000 people voting for a bin! They need their heads twisting! Nigel’s party is the only one which can save this country.”

‌



The Reform leader’s financial matters were his own business, the dental practice manager and a retired council worker, said. “It’s not for us to decipher.” But deep down, Reform must have known Farage’s star was in danger of fading. The party did not spend more than £10,000 on social media adverts for nothing.

Outside a boarded up shop, Gemma Long, 48, told us she had boycotted the vote. “And if I had voted, it wouldn’t have been for Nigel Farage,” she said. “What that £5 million could have done here! The bank I worked in closed down, and I don’t have a job now. We need new jobs, new shops, look at the place. Why didn’t he spend the £5 million on Clacton?”

View 6 Images Dionne Marsh and husband Tom told us the right man won (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

Hairdresser Sue Jacobson, 66, hadn’t voted either. “I used to like Nigel Farage, but I’m not sure any more,” she said, sitting in the sun with her tiny dogs Milo and Tilly. “They are all the same in the end.” Ed’s taxis’ advertised ‘lady driver’ Jean Linton, 73, seemed to have Count Binface waving from her dashboard, alongside a Lucky Cat and a New York taxi. “That’s not Binface, it’s the Tin Man,” she said indignantly. “I voted for Farage. Maybe he can do something for Clacton.”

‌



Arriving in town via a train track lined by dusty buddleja, a world away from crypto billionaires, it was clear the celebrity Farage factor that once made an overlooked place feel a bit famous, has now turned sour for some. “It’s a circus!” one woman said, as she attempted to remove a neon inflatable ring from her son’s neck. “How would you like it?” Her friend added: “He’s made us a bloody laughing stock. Who am I supposed to vote for, an actual bin?”

In yet another surreal twist, last night saw Mr Farage triumphantly boycotting his own by-election – a vote nobody wanted except him, and which has already been boycotted by every major party. The police denied telling him not to attend. A speech Farage was due to give on Clacton Pier this morning was also cancelled. “I think it’s a disgrace he didn’t turn up to his own vote,” 24-year-old Courtland Hollis, a carer for his mum, Kelly, said. “He makes all this fuss and then spends all his time abroad anyway.”

View 6 Images Kelly Hollis with her son Courtland in Clacton-on-sea (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

Over the last few weeks, as their former MP battled an intergalactic space warrior dustbin, there have been moments when this seaside town has faced a total eclipse of its dignity. No wonder that thousands of constituents like Courtland didn’t vote at all. While, somehow over the summer, Britain has got used to the prospect of man versus bin, perhaps the real insult to locals was the 32 other candidates standing in the election – not just Count Binface but Baron von Thunderclap, Howling Laud Hope, Woke Trump Carrzee and Nick the Incredible Flying Brick. The town with the longest pier had produced the longest candidate list in British history and a ballot paper almost a foot long.

‌



At the tail end of polling day, outside the 'Spoons, I found Alan Hope – aka Howling Laud Hope, one of three candidates standing for the Monster Raving Loony party. Alan seemed impatient with the attention around Binface, reminding me this was his 38th election. “This is a special one for me, as it means I will have stood the most times for any English parliament,” he said. “I’m also now the longest-serving political leader of all time, having just overtaken Clement Attlee.” He looked longingly at the Wetherspoons. “At least I won’t come last,” he added.

As the sun set on the Pier there were bin tribute acts gathering like some kind of surreal recycling festival. Around one corner, David Ashcroft, 51 from Cornwall, had built his own R2D2 Binface, which he was touring in his camper van. Around another, Roger Hartley, from the Bureau of Silly Ideas, had two wheelie bins which he was activating by remote control under the sign ‘Bins for Good’.

View 6 Images David Ashcroft from Cornwall built his own R2D2 Binface (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

Even some of Reform’s supporters seemed to have gone rogue. 80-year-old Alan Murray, a retired decorator, was protesting against the party requiring an email address. “This is a protest,” he said, simply, “against the intershit.” A big part of Mr Farage’s charm is a promise to return to a simpler yesterday when you could still smoke all over your kids. But this is probably about as peak nostalgia as you can get.

‌



Yet at the count last night, the utter silliness of many of the candidates contrasted poignantly with the scores of local people from the borough patiently counting hour after hour, doing their civic duty with pride. Democracy at its best, and its most ridiculous, all in one gymnasium.

View 6 Images Roger Hartley, from the Bureau of Silly Ideas, bin tribute acts (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

For all the talk about the circus enveloping Clacton, 19-year-old Max said he had enjoyed the fact the election had got people in the town talking to each other. “It’s been brilliant,” he said, “everyone has been arguing about politics, town has been really lively. It’s like the town my mum remembers. I expect that will go again now, but I hope it doesn’t.”

If Mr Farage is found guilty by the Parliamentary Standards Commissioner, the Clacton Circus will be back sooner than the rest of the town might like.

News.title: Arsenal artist leading anti-racism campaign inspired by Bukayo Saka gesture
News.content:
Arsenal artist leading anti-racism campaign inspired by Bukayo Saka gesture

Hand of Hope is an anti-racism campaign fronted by world leading artists, one of whom has recreated a powerful image of Bukayo Saka being consoled after the Euro 2020 final

View 2 Images Bukayo Saka was comforted by an England staff member after the heartbreaking Euro 2020 final defeat to Italy (Image: PA)

An anti-racism campaign inspired by a touching gesture caught in the aftermath of England's defeat to Italy at the Euro 2020 is raising funds to fight back against vile abuse.

‌



The campaign, Hand Of Hope, is fronted by world leading artists including Hayden Bone, who has been Arsenal's official club artist for the last five years. Of the 39 pieces of art which is set to go under the hammer, Bone has contributed eight to the collection, including one featuring Bukayo Saka.

‌



The Arsenal star was subjected to horrific racist abuse online after missing a penalty in the shootout that would have seen England land just a second major trophy with victory. Jadon Sancho and Marcus Rashford were also abused after missing in the shootout.

‌



Saka received a tremendous swell of support following the ugly abuse and the recreation of an image of him being comforted following the shootout will now aid attempts to raise up to £100,000 for causes including anti-racism and the encouragement of youth art worldwide.

Galatasaray reject £111m Victor Osimhen transfer offer as Arsenal task made clear READ MORE :

Bone said: ”I couldn’t be more strongly in support of Bukayo and the defeat of racism. I have painted him many times. He is a kind and thoughtful man who has endured a lot in his short life. He was victimised in an utterly despicable manner, and to come through stronger is a mark of the man. He is exceptional. These paintings are a fitting tribute to him and all the other great athletes who have overcome the sickness of racism.

“Art at this scale will keep the spotlight on the battle against racism. And there’s no better place to start than at school. Kids are blind to differences. If their heroes can inspire them to paint, support a better world, then we can make progress.”

‌



It was a moment in the aftermath of England's penalty shootout defeat to Italy that inspired the collection. Omar Meziane, England's Head Athlete Performance Chef at the time, was seen offering support to Saka by placing his hand on the attacker's shoulder as he digested the events that had just occurred.

View 2 Images

The gesture was snapped by a photographer and quickly went viral around the world.

‌



Meziane, who now holds the same role at Nottingham Forest, added: ”It was a moment frozen in time, a natural reaction. The entire camp had grown very close, which was entirely down to the manager, Gareth Southgate. We really believed we would win. Then the cruellest of endings.

”I saw Bukayo in the moment of despair, alone, utterly crestfallen. He felt my hand on his shoulder, turned to face me, simply nodded in response, no words. His eyes were empty, I knew what was coming, I saw the picture splashed across the media the next day. By then all hell had been unleashed on him.”

The collection of 39 exclusive paintings feature stars from all different sports who have been subjected to racial abuse but fought back. They include Saka, Tiger Woods, Thierry Henry, Serena Williams, Chris Gayle, Vinicius Junior, Neymar and Lewis Hamilton. They all feature in a centrepiece “statement painting” called “Remember Who You Are”.

News.title: King Charles opens historic part of Sandringham estate for overnight stays for first time
News.content:
King Charles opens historic part of Sandringham estate for overnight stays for first time

The monarch has opened The Water Tower, located on his vast Norfolk estate, for overnight stays for the first time since it was built in 1877

View 7 Images The King spends most of his time on the Sandringham estate (Image: Getty Images)

King Charles has started a ‘new chapter’ at the Sandringham estate, by opening one of its historic buildings for overnight visitors. The Water Tower has been transformed into a ‘retreat for two’, with bookings now available for the first time since it was built in 1877.

‌



The cosy rooms look over the picturesque 20,000-acre estate, with the news of the tower’s renovations being announced on social media. “THE WAIT IS OVER…Introducing The Water Tower,” read the caption on the Sandringham Instagram post. “Rising majestically above the Norfolk countryside on the historic Sandringham Estate, a remarkable piece of Royal history is being unveiled for a new chapter.”

‌



David Foster sets the record straight after claims he ‘snubbed’ Meghan Markle on the red carpet READ MORE :

7 View 7 Images The King has opened the Sandringham Water Tower for overnight guests (Image: Getty Images) 7 View 7 Images The tower first opened in 1877 (Image: sandringhamestate/Instagram)

‌



The tower was built in 1877 after the future King Edward VII and his eldest son, Prince Albert Victor, contracted typhoid at Sandringham and there were urgent concerns over water qualilty. Engineer James Mansergh was then commission to build the tower and it became a main source of supplying clean drinking water to the entire estate.

The Sandringham website states: “This extraordinary Victorian landmark has been thoughtfully restored into an exceptional retreat for two — bringing together Royal heritage, architectural grandeur and breath-taking views.

“Designed by renowned engineer James Mansergh, the Tower’s distinctive neo-Byzantine architecture, circular form and intricate brickwork have stood proudly above the Norfolk landscape for almost 150 years.”

‌



View 7 Images The cosy living room in the Water Tower (Image: Oliver's Travels)

The post concluded by encouraging royal fans to head to their website and book their stay at the ‘transformed landmark’. The Sandringham Estate website boasts that the Water Tower is “one of the most unusual and memorable stays in Britain”.

“Inside, the accommodation has been carefully designed to celebrate the building’s unique character,” the listing describes. “Heritage-inspired tones and neutral interiors complement the Tower’s original features, while reclaimed elements sourced from the wider Estate sit alongside thoughtfully chosen furnishings.”

‌



“Historic pictures and photographs depicting The Royal Family and Sandringham’s rich past create a strong sense of place, ensuring the story of the Tower remains woven throughout the experience,” it continues.

View 7 Images The tower was built after King Edward VII and his eldest son contracted typhoid (Image: Oliver's Travels)

“Private, atmospheric and entirely unique, The Water Tower is an exceptional retreat for couples seeking something truly out of the ordinary.”

‌



The Water Tower is spread across several floors, with the entrance, kitchen, dining room and bathroom located on the ground floor, while the king-sized bedroom with views across the state takes up the first floor.

The second floor features a cosy living room with fireplace and access to a rooftop terrace, which boasts 360 degree views of the Norfolk countryside.

View 7 Images The rooftop terrace boasts 360 degree views of the Norfolk estate (Image: Oliver's Travels)

‌



The terrace was once used by the Royal Family and their guests during shooting parties and picnics, where they would take in the same sweeping views across the Estate.

The Water Tower is the most intimate accommodation available on the Sandringham estate, with other homes, including The Folly and the Gardens House, can house six and eight people respectively.

The Water Tower at Sandringham is available through Oliver’s Travels, with weekly rates from £1,500 to £2,395.

‌



View 7 Images The tower is spread across several floors and can accommodate two guests (Image: Oliver's Travels)

Sandringham is one of two estates that the monarch privately owns, with the other being Balmoral in Scotland. The Royal Family gather at the Norfolk estate each December, as Christmas in Sandringham is one of many royal traditions.

Article continues below

The estate is filled with royal history, while also being home to Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, the King’s disgraced younger brother, who resides in Marsh Farm after being booted out of the Royal Lodge in Windsor last year.

News.title: Images show harrowing extent of Stourbridge fire as '20 to 30 homes destroyed'
News.content:
Images show the "apocalyptic" scenes from a fire which ripped through Stourbridge, destroying up to 30 homes.

More than 100 firefighters have been tackling the blaze with flames. Stourbridge MP Cat Eccles said she believes about "20 to 30 homes have been completely destroyed".

West Midlands Fire and Rescue were called to the Racecourse Lane area of Stourbridge at around 1.30pm on Thursday. It is believed the fire spread from grassland to buildings, forcing people to flee for their lives.

Tom Barnett, head green keeper at Stourbridge Golf Course, told the Mirror: “We had to run for it at one point... It was like a war film with ash and smoke and the intense heat. The speed of the flames were like a tidal wave.”

A total of 54 people have been treated by paramedics, including 19 who were admitted to hospital, after wildfires broke out across the West Midlands yesterday, the region’s ambulance service said.

News.title: Watch: 'Carnage' in Stourbridge as houses destroyed by fire
News.content:
Fire crews are continuing to tackle blazes in the West Midlands after multiple fires tore through the region on Thursday.

A number of house were destroyed by a fire in Stourbridge, with officials saying it is thought the fire started in nearby grassland before spreading to a residential area.

The BBC's Alison Freeman reports from the scene.

News.title: Farage faces renewed watchdog probe after Clacton by-election victory
News.content:
A parliamentary standards investigation into a Â£5m gift received by Nigel Farage has been reopened following the Reform UK leader's by-election win in Clacton.

The investigation into an alleged failure to declare an interest was paused after Farage resigned as an MP last month in response to scrutiny of his financial backing, triggering the by-election.

Farage won with 63% of the vote on a turnout of 44% in a highly unusual by-election that was contested by a record 34 candidates but was boycotted by all of the main Westminster parties.

Farage did not show up at the count, telling supporters Essex Police had warned him of an "organised campaign to disrupt and degrade the result".

He told supporters: "I'm damned if I'm going to stand on a stage, having won a resounding victory, a ringing endorsement of all that I've tried to fight for, and you've tried to fight for, and be demeaned and humiliated by nobodies, and I will not sadly be attending the count."

Reform UK cancelled what the party had billed as a "major speech" by Farage in Clacton on Friday morning and some scheduled media appearances.

In a statement, the Reform leader said: "The verdict is now in, and it is a convincing, overwhelming win, with more votes than we got in the general election of 2024.

"Today, the voters in Clacton have stuck up two fingers to the entire political establishment."

Farage received 22,239 votes, 1,014 more than his winning total at the general election in 2024, when he first became the MP for Clacton, and increased his majority from 8,405 to 12,784.

The turnout was about 14% lower than it was in the 2024 general election in the constituency but about average for recent Westminster by-elections.

News.title: Prisoners charged over attack on Sara Sharif's father
News.content:
Two prisoners have been charged with the attempted murder of fellow inmate Urfan Sharif who was jailed for the murder of his daughter Sara Sharif.

Steven Sansom, 47, and Adam Watson, 39, have also been charged with other offences relating to the incident in Belmarsh Prison on 1 January 2025, the Crown Prosecution Service said.

The men will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court for a first hearing on 26 August.

Sharif, 43, and Sara's stepmother Beinash Batool were sentenced to life imprisonment after being convicted at the Old Bailey of killing Sara at their home in Woking, Surrey.

News.title: Eurovision proposes new rules to reduce political voting
News.content:
Organisers of the Eurovision Song Contest are proposing major rule changes to discourage voting campaigns that aim to influence the results.

Under the current system, viewers can vote up to 10 times for their favourite act by phone, text message or online.

In a letter to participating broadcasters, the EBU reportedly suggested moving the vote entirely online and forcing the public to select their top three acts - instead of being able to vote multiple times for one contestant.

The EBU said politically motivated voting had become "persistent" and was seen by many as "deeply worrying". The voting rules have been under scrutiny since the Israeli government encouraged fans to register multiple votes for the country's contestant in 2025.

Yuval Raphael's song, New Day Will Rise, placed 15th with the contest's juries - but outperformed every other participant in the public vote, scoring 297 points. In the end, Raphael finished as the overall runner-up.

A number of broadcasters subsequently queried how Israel placed so highly. They pointed to the fact that official social media accounts linked to Israel's government, including that of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, had asked people to vote for Raphael 20 times, the maximum allowed.

News.title: Instagram accounts fuelling Ceuta crisis with paid advice for help to cross
News.content:
This weekend, Mohammed wants to travel from Morocco to the neighbouring Spanish enclave of Ceuta, on the northern tip of Africa.

He's a Moroccan man in his twenties and wants to emigrate to Europe - not least because he's been seeing lots of videos on Instagram that make the trip look easy.

He contacts several of the Instagram accounts and one replies, claiming to have helped "many people" and offering him advice on how to cross for hundreds of pounds.

Except Mohammed isn't real - he's a dummy account I've set up to investigate a network of interconnected Instagram profiles that are driving the influx of migrants to Ceuta with aspirational content and offering them help for a fee.

It comes after roughly 78,000 migrants from Morocco arrived by sea into Ceuta in a matter of hours last month, 100 of whom died according to the Mayor of Ceuta.

The crisis has calmed since, but it has sparked tensions between EU nations who share open borders as well as criticism of the Spanish government.

The BBC's Top Comment podcast has identified dozens of Instagram profiles that portray the short swim around the Morocco-Ceuta border fence as safe and easy - but in reality, people have drowned trying to make the crossing and take much longer routes. The accounts also wrongly show Ceuta as a viable route to mainland Europe.

Our research suggests that this has contributed to the influx, alongside other factors such as misinformation about changes to Spanish immigration law and allegations about weak border controls.

News.title: 'Glam helps mentality' says sprinter Amy Hunt, but can it give you that winning edge?
News.content:
They say practice makes perfect, but for some athletes that means more than just training to be as fast as possible.

For many, it's also about what you wear or how you accessorise with things like jewellery.

So can getting glammed up help your performance?

British sprinter Amy Hunt certainly thinks so, and it seems to be working as she's now secured two gold medals at the European Athletics Championships.

The 24-year-old, who's gunning for a historic quadruple win at the event this week, told BBC Newsbeat "the glam definitely helps that mentality because sprinting is such a confidence game".

"Everyone knows I love a bit of glam and I love my nails."

The Midlands-born athlete has curated her nail art to reference landmarks within Birmingham, where the competition is being held, including nods to the Jewellery Quarter and the Bull Ring, external.

Hunt says "looking good and feeling good" is all part of her process to get into the right mindset, and likens walking out on to the track to a gladiator entering an arena.

"It's a show at the end of the day," she says.

Fellow athletes, including Olympic champions Keely Hodgkinson and the United States' Sha'Carri Richardson and Noah Lyles, are among those who have also become known for their statement nail art on the field, but it's by no means a new practice.

US Olympic champion track star Florence Griffith Joyner, known as Flo-Jo, is often regarded as a pioneer of competing with long, vibrant nails back in the 1980s.

News.title: Mother jailed for killing baby by burning her with a hairdryer
News.content:
A mother who killed her baby daughter by burning her with a hairdryer has been jailed for six years.

Courtney Gartshore, 28, used the appliance to subject three-month-old Dahlia-Rose to "significant and sustained heat" on her head and body.

Emergency services were called to the scene at a property in Peterhead, Aberdeenshire, in September 2023, but the child had died.

Gartshore was convicted of culpable homicide - the closest equivalent to manslaughter in Scots Law - following a trial at the High Court in Aberdeen in July.

Sentencing Gartshore at the High Court in Edinburgh, judge Simon Collins KC told her, external she had inflicted "severe and disfiguring" burns on her daughter.

He said: "Given Dahlia-Rose's very young age, and the horrifying way that she died, this is a uniquely disturbing and distressing case.

"But it is tragic as well as terrible. And that is because the evidence suggested that the accused loved Dahlia-Rose, yet will have to live the rest of her life with the knowledge that she was responsible for her death."

News.title: Watch: What happens if Luigi Mangione pleads guilty today?
News.content:
The case of Luigi Mangione, who is accused of killing United Healthcare CEO Brian Thompson in New York, is back in the spotlight.

His lawyers are preparing to meet federal prosecutors Friday for a potential plea agreement, according to reports in US media.

Mangione faces two federal charges of stalking resulting in death, each carrying a maximum sentence of life in prison. It was not immediately clear which charges are under discussion.

He also faces a separate state trial over Thompson's death. He has pleaded not guilty to all charges in both cases.

The BBC's Nada Tawfik explains what could happen next.

News.title: NHS service admits data breach due to pager use
News.content:
The sensitive medical data of transplant patients from across the UK was routinely sent over an unencrypted pager network, an NHS service has admitted.

A BBC investigation found NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) sent the names, dates of birth and types of organs being offered or needed to members of hospital transplant teams who were using pagers, unaware they were not encrypted.

In 2019, then-Health Secretary Matt Hancock announced the NHS in England should stop using pagers by 2021, but some parts of the organisation have continued doing so.

NHSBT said it was "deeply sorry" and has reported the data breach to the Information Commissioner. It added it has now stopped sending patient data in this way.

Pagers are small battery operated radio receivers - popular in the 1980s and 1990s - that can receive short text messages, numbers to call, or alerts.

They are a one-way communication system and only able to receive messages, not send them, which was why they largely fell out of public use as more and more people started carrying mobile phones.

News.title: Final day of heatwave for many before weekend cooldown
News.content:
Kew Gardens in London reached 38.1C on Thursday, making it the UK's hottest day of 2026 so far, and the fifth hottest UK day on record.

It is also the second time this year that the temperature has reached 38C, after Lingwood, Norfolk recorded 38.0C on 26 June.

This is only the second time that 38C has been reached twice in the same year - the previous occasion being 2022.

Though the Met Office amber warning for extreme heat that covered large swathes of England on Thursday expired at midnight, high temperatures will linger in central and eastern parts of England on Friday.

Long spells of sunshine will lift temperatures to 29-34C (84-93F) across large parts of the Midlands, Lincolnshire, East Anglia and the south-east.

For many places it will mark a third consecutive day above official heatwave thresholds.

The heat will ease elsewhere.

Somewhat cooler conditions will begin to move into northern and western parts of the UK, although temperatures will generally remain above the norm for the time of year - widely reaching the low to mid-20s Celsius.

Many places will be dry with a mix of cloud and sunny spells although a few showers are possible, and these could be heavy and thundery in some places.

News.title: One million sign petition to keep PC Harper's killers in jail
News.content:
A petition to block the early release of PC Andrew Harper's killers has been signed by more than one million people.

The police officer, from Wallingford, Oxfordshire, died in 2019 when he was dragged by a car as three teenagers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers were sentenced to 13 years for his manslaughter in 2020 but could be released next year under plans to tackle prison overcrowding. The prime minister is looking at ways to keep them in jail.

Thames Valley Police (TVP) Federation acknowledged the important milestone the petition had reached "without fanfare" due to the seventh anniversary of the officer's death on Saturday.

The petition was started by TVP federation chair Aileen O'Connor who said the decision to consider the killers for early release "pours salt into wounds that have never healed".

She added it was an "insult to Andrew's family, his friends, his colleagues and the entire policing family".

The federation thanked all those who have signed in support.

News.title: Disability campaigners call for Burnham to delay assisted dying bill
News.content:
Disabled and terminally ill campaigners have written to Prime Minister Andy Burnham urging him to reform social and palliative care before assisted dying legislation is introduced in England and Wales.

The Assist Us To Live group says people are currently being "failed by society" and "introducing assisted dying in these circumstances will put sick and disabled people's lives at risk".

Burnham believes the funding of palliative and social care should be "fixed" before assisted dying is considered. The government is likely to remain officially neutral, but the PM's remarks suggest he personally will not back the bill proposed by Labour MP Lauren Edwards.

Bill supporters argue improving care services and giving terminally ill people "autonomy" over their final weeks must go hand in hand.

The proposed law - known as the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - would allow people over the age of 18 who were expected to die within six months to be given help to end their own life, subject to certain safeguards.

Having a disability in and of itself does not mean you would be able to seek help to end your life.

This is the second time a backbench bill like this is going through the House of Commons.

MPs voted in favour of a bill proposed by Labour MP Kim Leadbetter in 2025, but it was not passed by the House of Lords after an unprecedented number of suggested amendments delayed its progress until it ran out of time in April this year.

Edwards reintroduced an identical bill in June in order to "finish the job" started by Leadbeater. It is due to be debated in the Commons on 11 September.

Opponents of the bill believe the legislation has substantial flaws and would pose risks to disabled people, putting pressure on them to end their lives.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission, the UK's regulator, says legislation is "likely to have particular impacts on people with certain protected characteristics, especially older and disabled people, external".

Last year, the commission's chair Baroness Falkner said: "While the bill provides safeguards against a person being coerced or pressured to end their own life by another individual, we know that disabled people, older people and especially older disabled people, may feel pressured to prematurely end their lives by societal attitudes and a lack of the support and services they need."

Edwards has said there is time to improve end-of-life care before any assisted dying service would come into effect under her proposed law, given a four-year implementation period had been agreed in the previous debates.

News.title: Man died after being 'trampled' by cattle on estate
News.content:
A man injured in the grounds of a National Trust estate died from "severe chest injuries" after being trampled by cattle, an inquest has heard.

John Orton, 78, a retired telecommunications engineer, died at Felbrigg Hall, near Cromer in Norfolk on 13 July.

Assistant coroner for Norfolk, Maeve Sykes, opened an inquest into his death at Norfolk Coroner's Court on Friday and said a post-mortem examination gave a provisional cause of death as "severe chest injuries".

A National Trust spokesperson said: "We have been left shocked and deeply saddened by the death of a visitor who was seriously injured while walking at Felbrigg last month."

On 13 July, Norfolk Police were called to the estate at about 11:45 BST and said despite efforts to save him, Orton died at the scene.

Following the incident, the estate was closed while inquiries were carried out.

News.title: Brothers injured by 'exploding' steam room door
News.content:
Two children from Harrogate were hurt after a steam room door shattered while they were in Turkey on a package holiday.

The brothers, who were 11 and 16 at the time of the incident, were staying at the Green Nature Diamond Hotel with their parents. CCTV footage sourced from the hotel by their father shows the moment the glass door shattered, leaving them with cuts to various parts of their bodies.

Jet2Holidays initially denied liability, but later agreed to pay Â£7,000 compensation to the family.

The travel company said: "We would like to reiterate how sorry we are about this incident."

News.title: Killer who will not say where wife's body is to stay in prison
News.content:
A man who killed his wife and refuses to reveal where her body is cannot be freed from prison, after the High Court overturned the Parole Board's decision to release him.

Glyn Razzell, 66, was jailed for life in 2003 after being convicted of murdering his estranged wife Linda, who disappeared in Swindon the year before. He has never disclosed what he did with her body.

The Parole Board decided in April that Razzell could be released as his imprisonment was "no longer necessary" to protect the public.

It is the first time the Secretary of State for Justice's power to refer the decision to the High Court has been used to overturn a Parole Board ruling.

Announcing her decision earlier, judge Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb said: "I am not persuaded that the risk has diminished to such a level that offender management is capable of keeping the public safe if the defendant is released."

She referred to a history of intimate partner violence (IPV) and coercive control, noting that there were references recorded of Linda's "fear".

Judge Cheema-Grubb said Razzell "has a propensity to violence against women and that without some recognition of that aspect of his personality he remains a danger to women who come within his milieu".

His continued denial of the murder showed he is "not a man who will lightly admit when things start to go wrong in his life", she added.

She also said he could not be relied on to comply with licence requirements "especially when to do so might endanger his idea of himself as a victim".

News.title: 'Two out of four, baby' - Hunt wins 200m as she eyes historic quadruple
News.content:
Britain's Amy Hunt charged to 200m glory to secure her second gold medal of the European Championships - but the sprinter has her sights set on a historic quadruple in Birmingham.

The 24-year-old wants to "be iconic" and become the first athlete to win four European gold medals at the same championship.

And after triumphing in the 100m on Monday, she added another gold to her collection with a season's best time of 22.19 seconds in the 200m final on Thursday.

Hunt reeled in rival and compatriot Asher-Smith down the back straight to cross the line first.

"Two out of four, baby!" Hunt told BBC TV.

"This is becoming a magical week and one I will remember for the rest of my life."

Hunt is set to compete in the women's and mixed 4x100m relay events later and says there will be "no celebrations and no champagne until Sunday night".

"I have got a debt to the ladies," she said.

"We have got to come out here and make sure we show them who the best sprinting nation is in Europe."

Asher-Smith was beaten to silver by just 0.01 seconds by Ireland's Rhasidat Adeleke, who set a new national record.

"It unfolded exactly how I thought it would," two-time European 200m silver medallist Nethaneel Mitchell-Blake said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"I knew Dina would run a blistering bend and then say 'Amy, come and catch me'. And that's what Amy has done."

News.title: Pair charged with attempted murder after Sara Sharif’s father attacked in Belmarsh Prison
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

Two men have been charged with attempted murder after the father of murdered schoolgirl Sara Sharif was attacked in prison.

Steven Sansom, 47, and Adam Watson, 39, are accused of trying to kill Urfan Sharif at HMP Belmarsh on New Year’s Day last year.

The Crown Prosecution Service said the pair are due to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on August 26.

It is understood the charges relate to an incident in which Sharif was allegedly ambushed in a cell at the category A prison by two inmates armed with the jagged lid of a tuna tin.

Daren Streeter, deputy chief crown prosecutor at CPS London, said: “Our prosecutors have worked closely with the Metropolitan Police to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring the case to court and pursue criminal proceedings.”

The Metropolitan Police previously said officers were probing “an allegation that a prisoner was assaulted at Belmarsh”, adding that “the 43-year-old suffered non life-threatening injuries”.

The Sun reported that Sharif suffered cuts to his neck and face and received medical treatment inside the prison.

Sharif and Sara’s stepmother, Beinash Batool, were jailed for life in December for years of horrific “torture” and “despicable” abuse that culminated in the 10-year-old’s murder.

The court heard that she suffered “unimaginable pain, misery and anxiety” as she was repeatedly beaten, burned, bitten and restrained at the family home in Woking, Surrey.

Sharif was handed a minimum term of 40 years and Batool was given 33 years.

A state in India has suspended the licenses of four Domino Pizza outlets after reporting ⁠insect infestations as part of a food hygiene crackdown.

The license of one Pizza Hut store was also suspended as many products used were found to lack expiry dates, according to a note from ⁠the state's Food and Drug Administration ​about ⁠this week's operation.

Jubilant FoodWorks, which operates Domino's outlets in India, declined to comment, and ⁠Pizza Hut franchisee Sapphire Foods did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. ​Domino's ⁠Pizza Inc. and Yum Brands, which ‌owns Pizza Hut, did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

In recent weeks, India's federal food regulator has cracked down on labelling by companies ‌including PepsiCo and Diageo that it says breaches rules, ‌while also cancelling many food business licenses over poor hygiene.

Maharashtra, home to Mumbai, has seen its new food safety chief, Tukaram Mundhe, conduct raids and shut popular eateries, making him a ⁠social media sensation.

open image in gallery Scooters are parked outside a closed Domino's Pizza outlet after Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration found violations during an inspection in Mumbai, India, August 14, 2026 ( Reuters )

Many Indian roadside food and local restaurants have a reputation for poor food quality. On Tuesday alone, Maharashtra food officers inspected more than 100 outlets, and issued "improvement notices" to 95 of them.

Mundhe's department also inspected outlets of Domino's and Pizza Hut, foreign brands which have a reputation for maintaining stricter safety and hygiene protocols.

The government department said three Domino's ‌outlets in Mumbai and one in another city lacked proper pest ​control.

"The administration has a strict stance on the quality of food ‌items," Mundhe said in Thursday's ⁠note.

Footage posted online by Indian media outlets appeared to show at ⁠least one Domino's outlet's pizza oven containing heavy rust and a buildup of food and grease.

Over ‌the years, Domino's ​and Pizza Hut have become popular, with ‌outlets expanding fast into India's smaller ​cities. Domino's is also India's largest international fast-food and pizza chain, with around 2,400 outlets.

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal in talks with England defender and eye Osimhen, Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez deadline looms
News.content:
Arsenal have opened talks with Bayer Leverkusen over signing England international Jarell Quansah. The Premier League champions have been keen to sign a defender following the injury to William Saliba and the 23-year-old Quansah, formerly of Liverpool, would be able to cover both centre-back and right back positions.

The Gunners have also received interest in Gabriel Martinelli from Galatasaray, while the he availability of striker Victor Osimhen has been raised in those talks. Arsenal have also been linked with moves for Atletico Madrid’s Julian Alvarez and Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola as Arteta bids to add a marquee signing in attack this summer. Barcola also leads Liverpool’s list of transfer targets and the Reds remain in talks with PSG over a fee,

Meanwhile, Enzo Maresca has indicated that Manchester City will not buy Enzo Fernandez before Chelsea’s 5pm deadline and at their £120m asking price. It comes as Barcelona are set to make a third bid of around £60m for Rodri, but are still set to fall £10m short of City’s valuation of the Ballon d’Or winner. The deal could influence the speed of any move for Fernandez, with Maresca pushing for the midfielder's signature.

News.title: This central London hotel has an unbeatable view of Tower Bridge
News.content:

Overlooking London landmarks, this grand Four Seasons outpost has just the right amount of quirk not to feel stuffy or intimidating

Location

The hotel is situated across from Trinity Square Gardens in Central London, with views out towards the historic Tower Bridge as well as the Tower of London.

Four Seasons Hotel London at Tower Bridge is also a short walk from many of the capital’s hotspots. Restaurants, pubs and tourist favourites, including the stalls of Borough Market, are all a short walk distance away. Take a stroll across the historic bridge after dinner when the crowds have thinned out, or stop for a bite or a drink in one of the bars or eateries that are moments from the hotel.

The hotel is just a few minutes from Tower Hill Station on the Central and District Tube lines. It’s a 15-minute walk from London Bridge, which has National Rail services to southern counties including Kent, Surrey and Sussex, with stops including London Gatwick. It is around a 15-minute walk to Bank station, which connects to St Pancras International for more domestic routes across Britain, and the Eurostar.



The vibe

open image in gallery The exterior of Four Seasons Tower Bridge with its four columns ( Four Seasons )

The hotel is housed in an early 20th-century, neoclassical-style building with four imposing columns that are flanked by door attendants who offer a warm greeting. There is a nod to the hotel’s history with a small “museum” of objects that were found on the site during previous renovations.

Bombing in the Second World War led to the caving in of a domed roof that was replaced in what is now the central Rotunda Bar with a new glass dome which draws inspiration from St Paul’s Cathedral. This is the beating heart of the hotel – romantic and elegant with a Jazz Age feel.

Service

Service was excellent throughout my two-night stay, with luggage taken off my hands as soon as I approached the hotel, helpful suggestions made for wine at dinner, and staff being forthcoming about my last-minute request to move breakfast to room service one morning.

Bed and bath

There are 89 rooms and 11 suites, plus guest residences, spanning six floors and ranging from Standard rooms to Skyline Penthouses. Some rooms face into a futuristic-looking garden courtyard, though bear in mind that these are overlooked by all other rooms that face inside – so you may want to keep your curtains closed for privacy.

open image in gallery An elegant Primary room ( Four Seasons )

The rooms are tastefully decorated in neutral tones, with accents of gold. A curated selection of books, including British literary classics and interior design tomes, adds a homely feel. The suites have dining and lounge areas, and desks with custom stationary and postcards, as well as separate dressing rooms.

With marble and chrome, the bathrooms feel grand, opulent and spa-like. The huge bathtubs invite guests to take lazy soaks, and the heated floors coupled with soft robes and slippers make the post-bathing experience super relaxing, too.



Food and drink

The Rotunda Bar and Lounge is where breakfast is served along with drinks and afternoon tea. The breakfast buffet features perfect pastries and fresh berries, plus the elements of a full English. The iced latte was spot-on. The Chinese breakfast includes noodles, steamed buns and fresh fruit.

Mei Ume is the hotel’s Japanese-Chinese fusion restaurant. A second restaurant specialising in steaks called Cooper’s Cut opened earlier this year.

open image in gallery Sushi and dumplings at Mei Ume restaurant ( Four Seasons )

The tasting menu at Mei Ume is divine from start to finish, featuring sashimi, delectable traditional Peking duck pancakes, spicy dan dan noodle soup, a sweet flaky sea bass fillet and barbecue char siu-style pork. The restaurant itself is striking in its decor, with dark wood, jewel-toned cushions and Asian-inspired art including a giant red cat sculpture to welcome guests – which is the inspiration for the dessert that concludes the tasting menu.

Facilities

The enormous spa and wellness facilities, spanning over 18,000 sq ft, include a 24-hour gym equipped with Technogym equipment, a 14-metre lap pool, sauna and steam rooms, plus a vitality pool for deep relaxation including massage pods, neck massager and underwater jacuzzi beds.

The spa includes eight treatment rooms with a hammam suite with heated marble plinth for traditional Moroccan treatments and there’s even a sound pod for guided meditation sessions. With a hairdresser and nail salon on site too, you can have the full beauty works done without leaving the hotel.

Other facilities include valet parking, 24-hour room service, chargeable laundry and dry-cleaning and a complimentary shoe shine service.



open image in gallery Enjoy an afternoon tea with views over London landmarks ( Four Seasons )

Accessibility

There are wheelchair accessible entrances, and fully wheelchair and hearing accessible rooms available. They include lowered beds, chairs, light controls and roll-in showers.

Pet policy

Dogs and cats under seven kilos are welcome with no extra fee, but you must inform the hotel before your stay. There is a dedicated dining menu for dogs with meats and a side of your choice, starting at £14.

Check-in/check-out

Check-in is 3pm, check-out is 12 noon.

Family-friendly?

The hotel offers options for connecting rooms, which can be equipped with complimentary cots. Children under 18 stay free when sharing a room with their parents. Kid-friendly pool times are twice a day from 6.30am to 11am, and 2pm to 6pm. Kids receive welcome gifts on arrival. Baby bath tubs, bottle warmers and kids bathrobes can be provided.

At a glance

Best thing: The luxurious and deeply relaxing rooms.

Perfect for: Exploring central London’s tourist hotspots.

Not right for: A low-key stay.

Instagram from: The Rotunda Bar and Lounge during afternoon tea.

Address: 10 Trinity Square, London EC3N 4AJ

Website: fourseasons.com

Phone: 020 3297 9200

Samuel was a guest of the Four Seasons Hotel London at Tower Bridge

News.title: Europe on fire as record-breaking temperatures hit continent
News.content:
