Sports.title: Enzo Maresca tells his old club Chelsea he WON'T meet their 5pm deadline for £120m Enzo Fernandez transfer today as saga threatens to turn sour
Sports.content:
Manchester City will not meet Chelsea’s 5pm deadline to bid £120million for Enzo Fernandez.

New boss Enzo Maresca insisted that City will not be doing any incoming business before the close of play, while Rodri returned to the training ground for pre-season testing after back surgery.

Barcelona are attempting to thrash out a transfer worth more than £60million for the Spain captain, who held talks with his manager on Friday.

Fernandez wants a move to the Etihad Stadium this month, with Chelsea insistent that his future will be resolved before the weekend.

‘Not today to be honest, I don’t think we’re going to do something today,’ Maresca said, while opening the door to more big-name departures out of City this month.

Tijjani Reijnders is putting the finishing touches to a £52m switch to Al Qadsiah in Saudi Arabia, while Savinho wants to join Tottenham.

Enzo Maresca has said he won't adhere to Chelsea's deadline over a move for Enzo Fernandez

Maresca is overseeing a midfield rebuild at City after replacing Pep Guardiola this summer

Maresca – who heads into his first competitive fixture with the club in Sunday’s Community Shield against Arsenal – has suggested that there could be further outgoings in the coming weeks.

‘We’ll see what happens with some more, there is a change in this moment,’ the Italian said. ‘We are in a moment where players that were here many years have already left or [others who] probably can leave.

‘And that means there is a change. We're going to try to do our best. At the moment the transfer window closes, we need to be good enough to find as soon as possible solutions for the team.’

The 46-year-old refused to discuss players from other clubs, adding that ‘I don’t think it’s good when people from other clubs speak about our players’ after a summer of discussion around Rodri in Spain.

Reijnders had decided to pursue other opportunities after a lack of starts last season and Maresca believes there are others in the same boat.

‘They all work every day, they all do sessions every day and at the end of the week they all want to play a game,’ he said.

‘When they don’t play, they struggle to understand or they struggle to see the reason why and I can understand that after one season some of them would like to play a little bit more.

‘It’s a bit difficult to convince players when they are already convinced. You need to change their thoughts, that is not always easy.

‘Tijjani’s situation is like James Trafford’s situation and some more players but I think when the club, the player, the manager, they all think the same way, that probably the best decision for a player is to go, you have to go.’

Sports.title: 'We've seen the script written for us but we're here to prove them wrong': Lincoln's joint-managers Tom Shaw and Chris Cohen on sharing the 'chaos' together, why they know their dynamic works and the Imps' transfer plans
Sports.content:
When Michael Skubala left Lincoln City for Bristol City in June, the club had a decision to make.

Skubala had overseen an incredible two-and-a-half years at the ProAmpac Stadium, guiding the Imps to the League One title with 103 points last season and promotion to the second tier for the first time in 65 years.

But Lincoln’s rise from the National League to the Championship has been built around a unified, club-wide strategy that is bigger than any one person - in an environment where staff are given the opportunity to develop.

So, while interviews took place with outside candidates, Lincoln took the bold step of promoting Tom Shaw and Chris Cohen to joint-head coaches.

Shaw joined Lincoln's academy in 2018 and had a seven-game spell as caretaker boss before Skubala’s arrival in 2023. Cohen, in his third spell with the club, had been joint-assistant head coach alongside Shaw since November 2024.

Both had significant responsibility under Skubala, regularly taking training sessions, leading meetings and helping to develop Lincoln’s game model.

Lincoln City appointed Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw as joint-head coaches earlier this summer

The unique and bold move came after boss Michael Skubala left the club to join Bristol City

A single head coach was considered, but the club felt the partnership best suited their collaborative approach. More importantly, they believed it offered the best way to preserve the structure behind such a special campaign.

‘There are a few more things like this to do,’ Shaw tells Daily Mail Sport about his newfound media responsibilities. 'It’s been very similar on the pitch, but a few more roles off it, which have been really good challenges.’

Ironically, the idea of becoming joint-head coaches was one Shaw and Cohen had already discussed in the event Skubala left, but the club beat them to it.

‘They'd thought of it first,’ Cohen says. ‘So we never had to ask for it. They came to us and said, "This is the way we see it happening if you two are both happy to do it that way”.

‘And I couldn't think of a better person to be sharing the chaos of being a manager in the Championship with.’

The appointment has inevitably sparked debate. Peterborough owner Darragh MacAnthony this week said he ‘hated’ the idea of joint-managers, insisting there ‘can only be one’ and argued the model is ‘problematic’.

‘We appreciate the question marks because it's not the norm,’ Shaw says. ‘But this is a way of working that we've been doing for a number of years that has brought big success.

‘Everybody in the building knows how it works, why it works, and we'll be continuing that. We’ll share duties between us, and, over time, figure out who's better at each of them.

‘But we've known each other for a long time, and we've earned this opportunity to do it together.’

Lincoln won the League One title with 103 points after an incredible unbeaten run last season

They are sticking with the players who won them promotion, meaning stars like Reeco Hackett (pictured) will get a chance to thrive in the Championship

Managing in tandem remains unusual, and critics will point to the infamous failed experiment when Liverpool paired Gerard Houllier with Roy Evans in the 1990s.

But Cohen and Shaw insist their arrangement is fundamentally different. And, listening to the pair explain their relationship, it is easy to see why Lincoln believe the model can work.

‘For the last three seasons, we've been designing a game plan throughout the week,’ Cohen says. ‘We would then go to Michael with it, and he had the final say.

‘By the time we went into the room, we were united. We got there through a load of disagreements and debates, but the main thing was we would live by it on a Saturday. By the time we’d leave the analysis room, we’d be completely convinced.'

Their relationship goes beyond the training ground, too.

Shaw, who has driven in with Cohen for the past three years, says: 'We've grown to love each other's company and there is massive respect.

‘I watched Chris play back in the day so I have huge respect for him as a football man and just as a bloke in general.

‘We’ve got a really nice relationship, and our families know each other now too, which is another lovely thing.’

Cohen and Shaw were key cogs in Skubala's coaching team, and they are relishing the step up

The Imps are back in the second tier of English football for the first time in 65 years

The appointment also provides continuity after a campaign that ended with Lincoln on a club-record 29-match unbeaten run. That became 30 with Saturday’s 2-1 Carabao Cup victory over Derby.

Several members of the promotion-winning squad have signed new deals and, while key man Jack Moylan moved to Cardiff City, five players have come through the door, including highly rated Tottenham forward Mason Melia, who had been the subject of 30 loan enquiries.

‘We don't want to be one of these clubs that moves up a division and clears the decks to try and get players they think are going to be better,’ Cohen says.

‘These players are capable in the Championship. They got 103 points last year, which should give them an incredible amount of confidence.

‘There's some big names in the division, some experienced managers we've got to go toe-to-toe with, but we feel prepared. The players deserve to go and push themselves and see how they can do at this level too.

‘There will be some tough weekends but our job is to keep the belief in this group because we know they’re good enough.’

Lincoln had the 17th biggest budget in League One last season and are likely to be among the Championship’s smallest spenders. Yet they are prepared to be ambitious in the transfer market.

The Imps have already broken their transfer record for Romanian defender Andrei Coubis and are likely to do so again before the window closes.

They remain the overwhelming bookies’ favourites for relegation, but Shaw and Cohen are relishing the opportunity to silence the doubters.

‘We've seen the script that's written for Lincoln City in the Championship,’ Shaw says. ‘That’s a massive motivation for our lads.

‘We're here to prove people wrong every week and this club has done pretty well as the underdog in recent seasons.’

Lincoln extended their club-record unbeaten run to 30 games with a 2-1 victory over Derby

Cohen and Shaw celebrate after the impressive season-opening win in the Carabao Cup

Whatever happens, it will be a journey for the thousands of Lincoln fans who will follow their team around the country and watch them face sides they could have previously only dreamed of meeting in a league match.

It starts with Middlesbrough on Saturday.

‘We’re hopefully going to win lots of games, but we’ll also lose and draw lots,’ Cohen concludes. ‘But at the end of every game we have to make sure we've put in a performance that everyone can be proud of.

‘If we walk off the pitch feeling that it is a team we can be proud of, that will be enough. There will be days where the ball wazzes in the top corner a couple of times, and there's not much we can do. But if it's something within our control, and we do it incredibly well, we're going to overachieve again.’

Shaw adds: ‘We've got some trips to some big names and stadiums, which will feel very different, but we have no fear.

‘We want to go and have a real ding-dong at some of these ex-Premier League and big football clubs.’

Sports.title: Arsenal interested in signing England international Jarell Quansah, 23, from Bayer Leverkusen
Sports.content:
Arsenal interested in signing England international Jarell Quansah, 23, from Bayer Leverkusen

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Arsenal hold an interest in Jarell Quansah and have made contact with the England defender's representatives.

Bayer Leverkusen do not wish to sell the 23-year-old but Arsenal want to be aware of the parameters and also know he would be open to joining them.

Arsenal are continuing talks for Ezri Konsa but Aston Villa's valuation has been prohibitive for the deal they want.

A Liverpool academy graduate, Quansah joined Leverkusen from his boyhood club last year. Liverpool had a buy back clause this summer, which has now expired, and they have no plans to bring him back.

Their priority remains forward positions and notably Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola.

Quansah made three appearances at the 2026 World Cup, and can play at centre back and right back.

Quansah made three appearances at the 2026 World Cup, and can play at centre back and right back

With William Saliba facing a lengthy injury absence, the Gunners are chasing reinforcements at the back.

Their pre-season form has further illuminated Saliba's absence, conceding an uncharacteristic number of goals, recently losing to Borussia Dortmund 3-2.

Quansah impressed for England at this summer's tournament in the United States, Canada and Mexico. After coming in to replace the injured Reece James at right back against Panama, he earned a starting spot in Tuchel's starting XI for their Round of 16 match against Mexico.

His red card for a high challenge on Jesus Gallardo ruled him out of the Norway quarter-final victory and Argentina semi-final defeat. He returned for England's third-placed match against France, and played 83 minutes as Tuchel's side won 6-4.

Quansah broke through into Liverpool's first team in 2023-24, but was limited to just four appearances in the top-flight in the side's title-winning campaign the subsequent season.

He was brought in to Leverkusen by former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag last July, signing for £35million.

In his debut season in Germany, Quansah made 44 appearances and scored five goals as Leverkusen finished sixth in the Bundesliga. He has also established himself in the England squad and has earned six caps.

Sports.title: Boxing champion Prichard Colon dies aged 33, 11 years after taking 'illegal' punches in fight which left him in a 221-day coma and a vegetative state
Sports.content:
Boxing champion Prichard Colon dies aged 33, 11 years after taking 'illegal' punches in fight which left him in a 221-day coma and a vegetative state

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former boxer Prichard Colon has died at the age of 33 more than a decade after suffering catastrophic brain injuries.

Back in October 2015 Colon, competing as a super-middleweight at the time, suffered a bleed on the brain after taking repeated blows to the back of the head during a contest with America's Terrel Williams in Virginia.

After vomiting and collapsing in the dressing room after his defeat, the Puerto Rican was rushed to hospital before spending 221 days in a coma. The fight with Williams had seen part of his skull collapse as a result of the repeated rabbit punches, which are deemed illegal in the sport.

After emerging from the coma, Colon, once a promising rising star in the ring, was left in a vegetative state with life-altering injuries. He was under the near-constant care of his family.

Colon conquered multiple national amateur championships and won a Youth Pan American gold medal before turning professional.

Colon's dad and former trainer, Richard, announced the heartbreaking news on social media, writing: 'Good morning, everyone. I regret to inform you of the passing of my son Prichard from this earthly world. He is now in a better place.'

He added: 'Thank you for so many years of love and prayers. As much as you can, please keep us in your prayers.'

Former boxer Prichard Colon has died at the age of 33, his family have announced

The Puerto Rican suffered catastrophic brain injuries during a 2015 fight (pictured)

Until that fateful fight almost 11 years ago, Colon had been one of the sport's most promising prospects.

He had established an unblemished 16-0 record with 13 knockouts with many in boxing viewing him as a future star.

Following the bout against Williams, Colon was rushed to the hospital where doctors discovered a subdural hematoma.

He underwent emergency surgery as medics desperately attempted to relieve the swelling in his brain. After spending 221 days in a coma, Colon awoke unable to walk or talk.

Despite the traumatic injuries, just three years ago, Colon had vowed not to throw in the towel.

In an update on his Facebook profile at the time, Colon attempted to speak with his mother and even raised a smile in a moving video.

The post was captioned: 'I will not give up'.

In other clips, the ex-fighter could be seen attending a truck rally with his family, while also appearing to take a positive step in being able to brush his own teeth.

He was left in a vegetative state and was under the near-constant care of his family

Until that fateful fight, Colon had been one of the sport's most promising prospects

His mother also shared a video of her son on his 31st birthday where she gave him a cupcake with a candle on it.

Colon's story is one of the most tragic in boxing history, with former heavyweight champion Deontay Wilder breaking down in tears while discussing it last year.

'We’ve seen what happens, look at Colon. How he got hit, Prichard Colon, correct,' Wilder said.

'This man didn’t have no kids… they don’t understand. Y’all don’t f****** understand what we go through, man.

'And I don’t even know him like that, but I will always be an advocate for us. Because this man will never know what it’s like to be somebody’s father. And that’s one of the most precious things in the world, to be somebody’s father. But he will never be nobody’s father, man.

'Because he got in the ring to support his family but now, his family got to take care of him for the rest of his life.'

Sports.title: Chelsea co-owner 'wants to sell up' as he faces investigation into multi-billion dollar loans - and has already ditched owning the LA Lakers for £9bn
Sports.content:
Chelsea co-owner Mark Walter has expressed an interest in selling his minority stake in the Premier League club, according to reports.

Walter, who has a 12.8 per cent minority stake in BlueCo, the consortium which owns Chelsea, has reportedly hit financial issues which have led to him selling the LA Lakers for a record £9 billion ($12.5bn). This comes less than a year after he bought a majority stake in the NBA franchise.

The US Attorney's Office is currently investigating how billions in loans extended to companies tied to Walter or his conglomerate, TWG Global, have wound up on the books of his insurance companies after passing through a third entity, according to the Wall Street Journal.

'Beyond the Lakers, Walter has also expressed an interest in selling his minority stake in the English Premier League club Chelsea, a person familiar with the matter said,' the report states.

According to Bloomberg, the FBI 'executed at least one search warrant' to seize a mobile phone. In a statement TWG Global, told the Financial Times it is 'aware of and cooperating with the investigation.'

US prosecutors are investigating companies run by Mark Walter, the billionaire owner of the Los Angeles Lakers and the co-owner of Chelsea

Josh Kushner (left), the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, has bought the Lakers from Walter for a record £9bn alongside former Disney CEO Bob Iger

Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, and former Disney chief executive Bob Iger appear to have swooped in at a convenient moment for Walter, and the deal for the Lakers is set to be the highest price ever paid for any sports team.

Walter, 66, made his money as one of the founders of bond manager and investment bank Guggenheim Partners in 1999. Beyond Chelsea, Ligue One side Strasbourg, which is also owned by BlueCo, and the LA Lakers, Walter also owns a stake in the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team, is the majority owner of the Los Angeles Sparks women's basketball team, and owns North America's top-level professional women's ice hockey league.

Walter became a minority owner of Chelsea as part of the consortium led by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital that completed the takeover of the club in 2022. Walter and Boehly both have a 12.8 per cent minority stake in the club, while Behdad Eghbali, who is co-founder of Clearlake, owns a majority 61.5 per cent.

Walter bought his LA Lakers share, reportedly worth an estimated £7.45bn ($10bn), a previous record, from the Buss family in October 2025.

He said: 'Owning the Los Angeles Lakers has been one of the great honours of my life.

'It has been an extraordinary investment, but what I will carry with me is the community, the fans, and a city that treats this team as family.'

The deal involving Kushner comes after he was part of the recent controversy surrounding FIFA president Gianni Infantino and an aborted plan to sell off stakes in the governing body's competitions to private investors.

Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Kushner, was expected to lead the proposed investor group for the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

Sports.title: Eva Carneiro's life now after Jose Mourinho Chelsea row and net worth as football club owner
Sports.content:
Eva Carneiro's life now after Jose Mourinho Chelsea row and net worth as football club owner

Eva Carneiro was once a key part of Chelsea's medical department, but her Stamford Bridge career came to an abrupt halt after an infamous row with Jose Mourinho in 2015

View 4 Images It's been over a decade since Eva Carneiro's infamous bust-up with Jose Mourinho (Image: Getty Images)

It was the moment that shattered the illusion of harmony at Stamford Bridge - and 11 years later, the echoes of one of the Premier League's most notorious touchline bust-ups are ringing loud once again.

‌



Thanks to a newly released 'Mourinho' Netflix documentary, centred around the career of managerial titan Jose Mourinho, the infamous 2015 clash between the former Chelsea manager and the club's then-team doctor, Eva Carneiro, has been thrust back into the spotlight.

‌



In the programme, Mourinho doubles down on his actions, backed by former Chelsea captain John Terry. But Carneiro, who has spent the last decade rebuilding her life and career away from the harsh glare of the media, isn't taking the comments sitting down.

‌



Here is a look at what actually happened, how Carneiro responded to the new documentary, and what her life - and bank balance - looks like today.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Cristiano Ronaldo married in front of just FOUR witnesses and signed pre-nup READ MORE :

Eva Carneiro slams Jose Mourinho and John Terry after Netflix dredge up Chelsea controversy READ MORE :

The infamous 2015 bust-up

The incident that derailed Chelsea's 2015/16 season occurred on its very first day. The defending champions were drawing with Swansea City and were already down to 10 men after goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was sent off. When Eden Hazard went down injured, Carneiro and physio Jon Fearn rushed onto the pitch to treat him.

‌



Mourinho was incandescent. By receiving treatment on the pitch, Hazard temporarily had to step to the sidelines, leaving Chelsea to defend a counter-attack with just nine men. After the match, the Portuguese manager publicly threw his medical staff under the bus, branding them "impulsive and naive."

Carneiro was subsequently stripped of her first-team matchday duties. A month later, she resigned, sparking a bitter and high-profile legal battle.

View 4 Images Jose Mourinho and Eva Carneiro infamously fell out in 2015 (Image: BPI)

‌



The £5m last laugh

While Chelsea's season spiralled out of control - culminating in Mourinho's sacking just months later - Carneiro took her fight to an employment tribunal. She filed a claim for constructive dismissal against Chelsea and a separate personal claim against Mourinho for sex discrimination and harassment.

Court documents revealed she rejected a £1.2million settlement offer, demanding a formal apology and proper compensation for the distress caused. Just moments before she was due to testify in 2016, a confidential settlement was agreed upon. Reports widely indicated the payout was in the region of £5m.

Crucially, Chelsea issued an unreserved public apology, stating unequivocally that Carneiro was simply following the rules of the game and fulfilling her duty of care as a doctor by putting the player's safety first.

‌



View 4 Images Carneiro was ultimately awarded a £5m pay out (Image: Getty Images)

Life now: net worth and football club ownership

Since leaving the Premier League, Carneiro, now 52, has thrived. She established her own private practice, the Sports Medical Group, located on London's prestigious Harley Street. She also acted as a private consultant for the Aspetar Orthopaedic and Sports Medicine Hospital in Qatar ahead of the 2022 World Cup.

She hasn't completely turned her back on English football, either. In 2024, Carneiro transitioned from club employee to club owner, becoming an investor in semi-pro side Lewes FC. The Isthmian League club is famous for its pioneering stance on equal pay for its men's and women's teams. Carneiro shares the boardroom with other high-profile investors, including Andy Murray's mother, Judy, and British musician Kate Nash.

‌



Thanks to her lucrative private practice, successful business investments, and her substantial Chelsea settlement, Carneiro's net worth is currently estimated to be around £3.8m.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Firing back at the Netflix doc

Mourinho's recent Netflix feature saw the 'Special One' refuse to apologise, claiming his "eyes know when a player is injured" and suggesting his anger was entirely justified. The Real Madrid boss said it was "very, very simple" to understand that Hazard wasn't really injured and didn't require treatment.

‌



Terry added that there was an unwritten "understanding" among players and staff that medics wouldn't enter the pitch unless an injury was obviously severe.

Carneiro, however, immediately took to social media platform X to set the record straight, quoting the General Medical Council (GMC) guidelines on a doctor's absolute duty of care.

View 4 Images Mourinho defended his actions in the new Netflix documentary about his career (Image: Courtesy of Netflix)

‌



"11 years on and here we are reliving the worst. Hope they made some money," Carneiro wrote, alongside a photo of her time at Chelsea. Targeting Terry's comments, she added: "We are bound by a medico-legal code of conduct. Genuinely it would be healthy for John Terry to learn the rules of the game. It's been long enough mate."

Breaking down the reality of the incident, Carneiro explained that her hands were tied the moment the referee requested her presence.

"When the medical team, at any level of football, are requested to attend a player by the referee, it is their absolute duty of care to attend and assess the player," she wrote, quoting GMC guidelines. "This is governed by standards of medical practice issued by the General Medical Council (GMC). A club official should have no say in this matter and the stage of the game has no relevance on the decisions of the medical team acting within the GMC code of practice.

"To discourage a doctor's duty of care to an athlete shows a disregard for player welfare and good medical practice. It is important that all responsible bodies continue to engage with the medical profession in order to establish this principal across all levels of the game."

She then wrote: "So IT IS really simple. Referee Michael Oliver called us on TWICE, player Eden Hazard requested medical assistance we then made eye contact from side line and he confirmed he needed medical assistance, TWICE. At that point my hands are bound as a medical professional."

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn's Teramoana Teramoana prediction will become much clearer with next fight
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn's Teramoana Teramoana prediction will become much clearer with next fight

Teramoana Teramoana is being tipped for a title shot within five fights by Eddie Hearn, but he's got to prove himself against a greater calibre of opponent

View 2 Images Eddie Hearn has high hopes for Teremoana Teremoana

The Olympians are coming. Teremoana Teremoana looked spectacular on the Gold Coast this week, making DeAndre Savage his 12th straight victim, all inside two rounds.

‌



The Australian lost to Bakhodir Jalolov in the Paris quarters two years ago, but looks to be adapting to the pro ranks quicker than the double Olympic champion.

‌



Part of that is due to Jalalov contesting two Olympic cycles. Now that his career is being guided by Queensberry Promotions, who have arguably the best crop of heavyweights in the world, the giant Uzbek will be looking to get things moving.

‌



Teremoana is part of rival Matchroom’s stable, which adds to the competitive dynamic and dangles the prospect of a world title rematch between the two Olympians down the line.

Tyson Fury sent clear message as Kristian Prenga sums up Anthony Joshua power READ MORE :

Dana White makes strange excuse for not having ring card girls at Dublin boxing event READ MORE :

Jalolov had just too much experience for Teremoana over three rounds in Paris. That won’t mean much should they meet in the pro ring.

Matchroom chief Eddie Hearn is talking about a world title shot at the back end of next year for Teremoana. That is ambitious even for a ruthless finisher like him. Bigger tests will come but he is certainly exciting. And at 28 looks set to forge a big career.

‌



Teremoana has the power to take out anyone and looks really organised behind the jab. The fundamentals are excellent. I particularly like the way he follows through after landing a big shot. He stays on top of his opponent and throws great combinations.

We have seen excellent Polynesian fighters before but I’m not sure we have witnessed a heavyweight from the south seas as exciting as this. Joseph Parker, a former world champion, of course, has all the tools but never looked as explosive as Teremoana appears.

View 2 Images Teremoana Teremoana produced a statement victory on the Gold Coast

‌



David Tua had a decent career, yet he was eight inches shorter and stocky, the opposite of this guy, who stands 6ft 6ins and weighs 19 stones.

Though there are some terrific athletes from the region, most look to rugby to forge a professional sports career. Teremoana could put a serious dent in that tradition.

I know the importance of rugby in New Zealand, where many of the Polynesian community play, but not even the great All Blacks bank what Teremoana will earn should he go all the way.

Article continues below

It’s still early, of course. The elite guys are not easy to hit, and they can take a shot. Hearn thinks Teramoana is five more fights from a title shot. To make good on that claim Teremoana, like every prospect coming through, must prove himself against opponents good enough to fire back.

Sports.title: Darts icon Bobby George opens up on his health after being told he could've been dead in 18 months
Sports.content:
Darts icon Bobby George opens up on his health after being told he could've been dead in 18 months

Darts legend Bobby George has spoken about what led him to discover a health issue before undergoing a procedure

View 2 Images Darts legend Bobby George has discussed a health issue (Image: David M. Benett/Dave Benett/Getty Images for Fitzdares)

Darts icon Bobby George is recovering after recently undergoing a procedure to fix a heart valve. The 80-year-old revealed how he almost missed the doctor’s appointment that spotted the problem, which could have potentially ended his life within 18 months.

‌



The ‘Bobby Dazzler’ has remained a household name for decades, having officially called time on his professional darts career in 2009. He twice reached the BDO World Championship final at Lakeside but lost to Eric Bristow and John Part in 1980 and 1994, respectively.

‌



George has subsequently thrived as a pundit, having begun working for the BBC in 1998. Still one of the sport’s biggest personalities, the icon’s smiling nature and enthusiasm for the game have ensured his enduring popularity.

‌



However, George recently faced a health scare after being alerted to a problem with his heart. The 80-year-old is currently resting up after undergoing a transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), rather than open-heart surgery, following an hour-long procedure which saw the implant inserted through his groin.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

“I was chatting to my doctors and said I want to live to f****** 90,” he told The Sun. “And when I’m 90, I want to live to 100. Maybe 180 is too much. I already look like a f****** dried-up doughnut now – one with no jam in it.”

‌



It transpired that George should have had his heart examined a decade ago and the doctor arranged for him to see a specialist. However, a letter with the details never arrived and it was only a stroke of luck that meant George made it to his appointment.

“Then my daughter, who lives with my ex-wife in Redbridge, rang to say she’s got a letter from the National Health Service for dad,” he explained. “It was an appointment, a time and date, with this specialist. They sent that f****** thing to my address from 40-odd years ago.

‌



“If I’d got a letter from the NHS not for me, I’d just f-ing bin it. And 99 per cent of people would, too. It’s like a Del Boy story really. Because if my daughter hadn’t lived at that address still, I’d be on my way to being dead.

View 2 Images George reached two world finals during his playing days (Image: Mark Leech/Offside via Getty Images)

Following the procedure, George is recuperating at his self-built, 18-bedroom mansion George Hall. He has been watching darts during his recovery and admits he was initially wrong about two-time world champion Luke Littler. The 19-year-old has clinched five major titles in 2026 and recently triumphed for England at the World Cup of Darts, alongside Luke Humphries.

“I said he could be a fluke. ‘Luke could be a fluke.’ But he keeps winning, and he ain’t no fluke,” George said of Littler’s success. “He’s unbelievable, isn’t he? He just wins everything. Just amazing.

Sports.title: Josh Kerr accused of 'ruining the sport' as feud reignites at European Championships
Sports.content:
Josh Kerr accused of 'ruining the sport' as feud reignites at European Championships

Josh Kerr's controversial decision ahead of the European Championships hasn't gone down too well with one of his colleagues

View 2 Images Josh Kerr has been accused of "ruining" long-distance running (Image: Getty Images)

Team GB star Josh Kerr has come under fire after skipping this week's European Championships. The 28-year-old Scot has been sensationally accused of "ruining the sport" by long-distance running rival Jakob Ingebrigsten.

‌



Last month, Kerr set a new world record for the men's mile in one of the athletics feats of the year. A few weeks later, he won gold in the same event at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

‌



Many had expected him to carry that momentum into the Euros, but the Olympic silver medallist decided to sit out the seven-day competition. "You can't hold that peak for that long," Kerr explained after insisting he had no regrets about his no-show.

‌



"I need to go back to the drawing board a little bit and give myself a bit of a rest. Or else I'm going to be flying close to the sun here."

However, his decision hasn't gone down well with Norwegian athlete Ingebrigsten, who feels that Kerr has damaged the event - and the sport - by not attending.

‌



"[I'm] very disappointed. And I think a lot of people should be, because that is what championships are all about," the 25-year-old told the BBC. "It's not for us as athletes to choose almost where to participate.

"We have these championships for a reason, and that is for the best athletes to compete - that is the whole point. "So I definitely think it is ruining the sport if we are not participating. We all have different plans, but I could never see myself in that position."

View 2 Images Ingebrigtsen and Kerr have been rivals for years (Image: PA)

‌



Tension between Kerr and Ingebrigsten is nothing new. Their rivalry dates back to 2023, when Kerr overtook the Scandinavian with 200 metres to go to claim the 1500m title at the World Championships in Budapest.

After the race, Ingebrigsten dismissed Kerr's achievement, insisting the Edinburgh native was "just the next guy." In response, Kerr labelled him "insecure."

The trash talk intensified in the buildup to the Paris 2024 Olympics. Ingebrigsten boasted that he could beat Kerr "blindfolded." However, Kerr won silver in the 1500m, while Ingebrigtsen missed out on a medal, finishing fourth.

Article continues below

Relations have generally cooled since then, but Kerr's absence in Birmingham threatens to reignite their long-standing feud in a big way.

Sports.title: Keely Hodgkinson's off-track life – marriage plans, behaviour remark, serious injury
Sports.content:
Keely Hodgkinson's off-track life – marriage plans, behaviour remark, serious injury

Keely Hodgkinson is the face of British athletics and the star of the European Championships in Birmingham, where she will try to beat the long-standing 800m world record on Friday night

View 4 Images Keely Hodgkinson is looking to become a three-time European champion in the 800m event (Image: Steven Paston/PA Wire)

Keely Hodgkinson has become one of the biggest names in British athletics, with her achievements on the track matched by a personality that has made her hugely popular away from it.

‌



The Olympic 800m champion will be back under the spotlight on Friday evening when she lines up in the women's 800m final at the European Championships in Birmingham, with a third successive title potentially within her grasp and the world record in her sights.

‌



At just 24, Hodgkinson has already packed an extraordinary amount into her career. Her gold medal-winning performance at the Paris 2024 Olympics cemented her status among the sport's elite, but her journey has also included painful injuries and difficult spells away from the track.

‌



Here, Mirror Sport looks at some of the biggest revelations surrounding the 2026 Sports Personality of the Year, exploring everything from her future personal ambitions to her inspiring resilience.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

What time is Keely Hodgkinson competing today? How to watch Team GB star READ MORE :

Keely Hodgkinson shows her class in BBC interview as result changed after appeal READ MORE :

Marriage admission

For all the success Hodgkinson has enjoyed professionally, she has made it clear that there are ambitions in her personal life that matter just as much. During an appearance on Welsh sprinter Jeremiah Azu's YouTube channel, she revealed that starting a family is among her biggest goals for the next decade.

‌



Asked what she wanted to achieve over the next 10 years, Hodgkinson admitted that marriage and motherhood were high on her list. "Mine is I'd like to start a family and get married. That's a big thing for me," she said.

She even gave herself a personal target, adding: "I'll be 34, I'd like to think I'd had a baby by then and I really look forward to that point of my life at some point."

View 4 Images Keely Hodgkinson says she wants to start in family in the next few years (Image: Domenico Cippitelli/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

‌



Her love life has previously been complicated by the demands of being an elite athlete. Hodgkinson was in a relationship with a fellow athlete for three years before the pair split in early 2024, with the pressures of a long-distance relationship proving difficult as their careers took them between Texas, Italy and London.

"Because I do what I do and put that first, we could go weeks, months and not see each other," she told The Times. "I'm not really interested in dating right now. I've never been on the apps. I like meeting people in real life."

Injury that left her unable to walk

Hodgkinson's remarkable ability to make the 800m appear almost effortless has sometimes disguised the physical punishment involved in competing at the highest level.

That was evident in July when she arrived at a Diamond League meeting in Eugene, Oregon, with her knees heavily strapped. She had suffered a serious fall just days earlier, with the damage leaving her struggling to move before eventually finishing second behind Lilian Odira.

Her condition became clear after the race, when Hodgkinson revealed just how badly the fall had affected her. "It's shocking, to be honest," she admitted. "Four days ago I couldn't even walk, so I guess I should take that into consideration but I wanted a lot more than that."

‌



View 4 Images Hodgkinson endured injury problems after winning Olympic gold at Paris 2024 (Image: Mustafa Ciftci/Anadolu via Getty Images)

The Olympic champion later posted a photograph on Instagram from a medical room, showing the bruising across her knees. Alongside the image, she wrote the determined caption: "Forward motion". The photograph prompted a wave of support from fellow athletes and fans, who praised Hodgkinson for competing despite the severity of her injuries.

It was another setback during an inconsistent period for the 800m star. She had already been forced to withdraw from the 400m final at the UK Athletics Championships in June after suffering what she described as a "little twinge".

‌



Despite the disruption, Hodgkinson's ambitions have remained unchanged. One of her biggest targets is still to break the 800m world record, which has stood since Jarmila Kratochvilova set the mark in 1983.

Behaviour comments

Hodgkinson has also attracted considerable praise for the person she is away from the athletics track, with World Athletics president and Team GB legend Sebastian Coe among those to have spoken particularly highly of her.

View 4 Images Seb Coe has lavished praise on Keely Hodgkinson (Image: Getty Images)

‌



During an appearance on the UNTAPPED podcast, the two-time Olympic 1500m champion called Hodgkinson "probably the most authentic person I currently know."

Coe recalled bumping into her at a Manchester restaurant while she was celebrating her birthday. Despite being only days away from winning her world indoor title, Hodgkinson was simply enjoying a normal night out.

"What you see with Keely is what you get. She is very funny, she's totally driven, but she puts things in perspective," Coe said. He went on to praise Hodgkinson for maintaining a sense of grounded normality despite her extraordinary sporting talent and fiercely competitive nature.

Article continues below

"She's just completely normal, but she is incredibly well talented. She's got a great coaching team around her. I'm probably going to lose whatever fan base I've got left in the south of England, but she's absolutely rooted to the north of England and that for me counts for a lot in life."

Sports.title: Jimmy Rimmer dies aged 78 as tributes paid to ex-Man Utd, Arsenal and Aston Villa icon
Sports.content:
Jimmy Rimmer dies aged 78 as tributes paid to ex-Man Utd, Arsenal and Aston Villa icon

Jimmy Rimmer, the two-time European Cup winning goalkeeper, has died at the age of 78 having enjoyed successful spells at Manchester United and Aston Villa

View 2 Images Jimmy Rimmer has died at the age of 78 (Image: Getty Images)

Jimmy Rimmer, the former Manchester United and Aston Villa goalkeeper, has died at the age of 78 as tributes are paid to the European Cup winner.

‌



The shotstopper was twice part of sides that ruled the Europe having come through the youth system at United. He was on the bench for their triumph in the 1968 European Cup final over Benfica.

‌



He moved to Villa in 1977, and that would see him enjoy the most successful period of his career. He made 229 league appearances for the Midlands outfit, and also played in every match of their European Cup-winning campaign in 1982. He was subbed off nine minutes into the final against Bayern Munich.

‌



It was during his three year spell with Arsenal that he made his solitary appearance for his national team, playing for England in a friendly against Italy.

View 2 Images Jimmy Rimmer claimed the European Cup on two occasions (Image: Bob Thomas Sports Photography via Getty Images)

‌



Aston Villa club paid tribute to the legendary figure as a statement read: "Aston Villa is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of European Cup winner Jimmy Rimmer, who has died at the age of 78. The thoughts of everyone at the club are with Jimmy's family and friends at this incredibly difficult time.

"Rimmer was one of the finest goalkeepers of his generation, and arguably one of the unluckiest when it came to big occasions. Despite collecting two European Cup winner’s medals, he wasn’t on the pitch at the end of either final."

His former United team-mate, Alex Stepney, said on social media: "Such sad news to hear Jimmy Rimmer has passed away, rest in peace and lots of love to Jimmy's family x".

Article continues below

Rimmer also had a three-year stint with Swansea City before fleeting spells with Hamrun Spartans in Malta and Luton Town, both in 1986.

Sports.title: Count Binface compares Clacton by-election to CARABAO CUP after winning 26 per cent of vote
Sports.content:
Count Binface compares Clacton by-election to CARABAO CUP after winning 26 per cent of vote

Count Binface came up against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage in the Clacton by-election, with all other major parties pulling out.

View 2 Images Count Binface has compared the by-election to the Carabao Cup after losing to Nigel Farage. (Image: Joe Giddens/PA Wire)

Count Binface has sent a warning to Nigel Farage, comparing his defeat in the Clacton by-election to the first leg of a Carabao Cup tie. Farage, leader of Reform UK, won the election with 22,239 votes.

‌



His main rival, a parody candidate, Count Binface earned 9.455 votes, 26 percent of the overall votes in a 44.4 percent turnout. Despite his victory, Farage did not attend the results declaration.

‌



Instead, he hosted his own 'Farage Fest' party. In a speech, he said: "I've been advised tonight by Essex Police that there is an organised campaign to disrupt and degrade the result that will take place in a few hours' time."

‌



Cristiano Ronaldo married in front of just FOUR witnesses and signed pre-nup READ MORE :

Paul Pogba's wife responds to retirement demand as Monaco contract set to be ripped up READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The by-election, which is estimated to have cost £250,000, has been labelled as a gimmick by all other major parties, who boycotted the race, leaving Count Binface as Farage's main rival The election came amid scrutiny over a £5million gift he received just before the 2024 general election.

Once Farage has been sworn in as an MP, an investigation into the gift is expected to open. If he is found to be in serious breach of the rules, then he could face a possible suspension, which would lead to another by-election in Clacton.

‌



It's something that Count Binface referred to when speaking to Sky News after Farage claimed victory. "You've just said at the beginning of this interview that Nigel Farage is claiming victory," he said.

"Well in that case it's going to be a two-legged match, like the Carabao Cup or the Cold War, because we're going to be back in a few weeks aren't we? We'll see what happens then."

View 2 Images Count Binface after the declaration of the Clacton by-election results. (Image: Joe Giddens/PA Wire)

‌



Speaking before the election about the resources put into it by Reform UK, Count Binface added: "Whether he's scared of me, you need to ask Nigel that, but I have noticed just how hard Reform have been campaigning against an alien space warrior with a Ceefax fetish who only eight weeks ago scored 0.2% [of the vote share] in Makerfield.

"So yeah, it's a curious... But I respect it, and I'm rather flattered."

When asked what a good result would be, he said: "Well look, a single vote, one precious vote, imagine one human like you going into that voting booth, getting the stubby pencil out, and choosing Binface instead of Farage.

Article continues below

"Just give yourself a moment to think about that. Anybody deciding they would rather vote for me to be Member of Parliament than Nigel Farage is a win. Now, you magnify that every single time there's an X for Binface and it mounts up, and it mounts up, and it mounts up.

"And I'll be interested to see the headlines you guys write with the number of people, percentage-wise, who make that decision."

Sports.title: Man Utd £42.7m boost as Liverpool make Ibrahim Mbaye decision
Sports.content:
Man Utd £42.7m boost as Liverpool make Ibrahim Mbaye decision

Manchester United have been linked with a move for Paris Saint-Germain winger Ibrahim Mbaye in the final weeks of the transfer window.

View 2 Images Manchester United and Liverpool have shown a transfer interest in Ibrahim Mbaye. (Image: Michael Reaves, Getty Images)

Liverpool have reportedly pulled out of the race to sign Paris Saint-Germain winger Ibrahim Mbaye, providing a potential transfer boost to rivals Manchester United. Both Liverpool and United have been credited with an interest in the Senegal international.

But they are not alone, with Bayern Munich, Porto, RB Leipzig, Bayer Leverkusen, Borussia Dortmund, Roma and Aston Villa all said to have made enquiries with PSG over his availability. It does, however, seem that Liverpool have dropped their interest, due to the cost involved.

It's reported by Fabrizio Romano on his YouTube channel that the club have held talks with agent Jorge Mendes over the possible transfer, but stepped away from a possible deal after being told it would cost €200 million (£171m) to sign both Mbaye and key target Bradley Barcola. Liverpool remain in talks with PSG over a deal for Barcola.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

While a deal for the Frenchman would account for the bulk of the figure quoted, reports suggest PSG are seeking between €40m-€50m (£34.2m-£42.7m) for Mbaye. It's a valuation Liverpool considers excessive, prompting them to drop their interest.

It's a development United could look to capitalise on, particularly given PSG's most recent transfer activity. The Athletic reports that the European champions have agreed a £42.7m fee with Barcelona to sign Ferran Torres.

His arrival at Les Parc des Princes is only set to further limit Mbaye's opportunities on the pitch and, consequently, make PSG more willing to consider a sale. AS reports that the club might even be prepared to approve a loan departure.

View 2 Images Ibrahim Mbaye is the subject of interest from several clubs in the transfer window. (Image: Jean Catuffe, Getty Images)

The winger remained on the bench throughout PSG's 2-1 European Super Cup triumph over Aston Villa on Wednesday night. This came despite him netting the team's goal in the 1-1 pre-season stalemate against United the weekend before.

Mbaye featured 31 times across all competitions last season, finding the net three times and registering two assists. Yet of those outings, only 11 saw him named in the starting XI.

He predominantly operates on the right flank, but is also capable of featuring on the left. Should United succeed in securing his signature, he will link up with the likes of Marcus Rashford, Bryan Mbeumo, Amad, Patrick Dorgu and Shea Lacey as wide attacking options for Michael Carrick this season.

United return to pre-season duty on Saturday when they face AC Milan (3.45pm kick-off), a fixture which could witness Rashford making his comeback for the club after returning from a loan spell with Barcelona.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
