World.title: Gusau’s resignation calls thicken after Super Falcons’ World Cup miss
World.content:
The calls for the resignation of Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) President Ibrahim Gusau have grown louder following the Super Falcons’ failure to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

For many Nigerian football supporters, the 2-1 defeat to South Africa in Thursday’s decisive play-off in Morocco was more than another disappointing result. It was the latest setback in a period that has left questions about the direction of the country’s football administration.

The defeat ended Nigeria’s enviable record of qualifying for every edition of the Women’s World Cup since the tournament began in 1991.

South Africa and Ghana have advanced to the FIFA Inter-Confederation Play-Off Tournament, while Nigeria’s qualification campaign is over.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

And with the NFF election less than two months away, attention has quickly shifted from the pitch to the leadership of Nigerian football.

‘He should resign’

On social media, some Nigerian supporters have called on Mr Gusau to step aside rather than seek another term.

One supporter, posting as @SarkinFoto, said the NFF president should submit a resignation letter instead of an apology.

“The NFF President needs to tender a resignation letter before daybreak and NOT an apology letter,” the supporter wrote.

Ben Marke was similarly blunt.

“In a sane society this guy ought to resign and apologize for wasting our time,” he posted.

Another supporter, @Weirdmaskman NG, questioned why Mr Gusau would remain in office after the latest setback.

“You don’t even have to clamour for his resignation. A responsible person would read the room and call it quits while he’s behind,” he wrote.

There were also stronger reactions.

“He should face jail time not just resign, very corrupt and incompetent NFF president,” wrote @Martins7906202, while The Beautiful Bald Man described Gusau as “grossly incompetent” and called for him to leave.

Olatunji Balogun was more direct in his submission.

“If FIFA wants to ban Nigeria the time is Now Because Gusau Must Go,” he wrote on his Facebook page.

These comments mirror the views of many other Nigerian football fans whose frustration is understandable in the context of the series of disappointments in the country’s football space.

For the second consecutive edition, Nigeria failed to qualify for the men’s FIFA World Cup after losing to DR Congo on penalties in the African play-off final in November 2025.

Nigeria will therefore miss both the men’s and women’s World Cups at the same time for the first time.

For a country that has traditionally expected its two senior national teams to be present at the biggest football tournaments, the double failure has become a major talking point.

Gusau defends NFF’s preparation

Before the decisive match against South Africa, Mr Gusau had already faced questions about the NFF’s preparations for the Super Falcons.

Speaking with reporters in Morocco, the NFF president defended the federation’s efforts to provide the team with competitive matches.

“Well, we are doing our best. You know, sometimes people just like to talk anyhow,” he said.

Mr Gusau pointed to the Falcons’ friendly matches against Cameroon as evidence of the federation’s preparations.

“If you can remember, between the period of November and March this year, we made the Super Falcons have a friendly match with the Cameroonian national team in Nigeria and in Yaoundé. And then, just about two months ago, we tried to organise a friendly match for them against the Senegal national team,” he said.

He also defended the decision to focus on African opposition rather than arranging matches against European teams.

“We are coming for an African tournament. Nobody should expect us to go and arrange a match for the Super Falcons against Norway or Sweden or what have you. We need to look at a competitive team from the African continent because we expect that along the line we can meet them and see what happens. At the end of the day, we met Cameroon,” he said.

According to Mr Gusau, arranging international friendlies for women’s teams in Africa comes with its own challenges, particularly the cost of moving teams around.

The NFF president also warned against what he described as uninformed criticism.

“So, people can talk anyhow, not mindful of what they are saying. But, as I have said earlier, we just want you to be patient with us, and we are very sure that, by the grace of God, the girls have now gained their strength and they will make a squad, and we’ll take it from there.”

The South Africa defeat, however, has given those earlier comments a new context, with critics now questioning whether the preparations were adequate to achieve the desired result.

A record of missed opportunities

The criticism of the NFF leadership goes beyond the two senior teams.

The Golden Eaglets have failed to qualify for three successive FIFA U-17 World Cup editions despite being five-time world champions at the level (the most successful team in the world).

With the Flying Eagles’ impending absence from the next Africa U-20 Nations Cup, hopes of featuring at the next U-20 World Cup is also in jeopardy.

WAFCON disappointment adds pressure

The Super Falcons’ World Cup failure came only days after another disappointing WAFCON campaign.

Nigeria entered the 2026 tournament as defending champions and one of the favourites, but suffered a shock 3-2 defeat to debutants Malawi in their opening match.

The Falcons eventually reached the quarter-finals but lost 1-0 to Cameroon.

That result ended their hopes of defending the title and forced them into the World Cup play-off route, where South Africa subsequently ended their qualification hopes.

The final outcome has therefore turned what could have been a difficult tournament into a much bigger leadership issue.

Gusau still wants another four years

Against this backdrop, Mr Gusau is preparing to seek another four-year term.

The NFF’s Elective Congress has been moved to 27 September in Lafia, Nasarawa State. The congress will usher in the federation’s Executive Committee for the next four years. The change from the earlier 26 September date was approved because the Super Eagles are scheduled to face Madagascar in a 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier on 25 September.

The NFF had earlier inaugurated its Electoral and Electoral Appeals Committees and pledged that the process would be free, fair and credible. Mr Gusau charged the committees to discharge their duties without fear or favour.

This creates an uncomfortable contrast for the incumbent.

While Nigerians are demanding his resignation, Mr Gusau is preparing to ask the NFF Congress for another mandate.

His administration can point to areas such as coaching education, competitions and football development as part of its record.

But supporters are entitled to ask whether those initiatives have translated into stronger national teams and a more successful football system.

Odegbami takes the battle to court

The leadership debate has also moved beyond social media.

Former Nigeria captain Segun Odegbami has announced plans to approach the courts over the NFF’s electoral process.

Mr Odegbami says he wants judicial clarification on the laws and regulations governing Nigerian football and believes the September election should be temporarily halted while outstanding governance questions are addressed.

His concerns include the structure of the NFF Congress, representation of state football associations, the role of government as a major funder of football and the structure and cost of NFF elections.

“Where we are now is the result of some faulty decisions at a point. Nothing illegal has happened. It is our choice,” Mr Odegbami said.

He said his objective was to seek “interpretation,” “transparency” and “justice” and help “steady this sinking ship of Nigerian football.”

His proposed legal action adds another layer to an already difficult election season.

Why Gusau cannot simply be removed

Despite the anger, there is a difference between demanding a resignation and legally forcing an NFF president out of office.

FIFA requires its member associations to manage their affairs independently and not be influenced by third parties. Article 14 of the FIFA Statutes specifically requires member associations to manage their affairs independently and provides for sanctions where that obligation is violated.

That principle is one reason the Nigerian government cannot simply remove an elected NFF president because supporters or public officials are unhappy with his performance.

The NFF leadership must ultimately be challenged through the federation’s own governance and electoral processes, subject to applicable law and the NFF Statutes.

This is where the September election becomes crucial.

The NFF Congress, rather than the wider Nigerian football-supporting public, will determine who leads the federation for the next four years.

So while thousands of supporters may demand Gusau’s resignation, the final decision on his political future within Nigerian football will be made through the federation’s electoral structure.

Beyond the noise

Shooting Stars Sporting Director Tobi Adepoju has summed up one of the biggest realities facing those calling for change: the NFF election will not be decided by social media.

“The NFF election does not have voters on social media. Sadly,” he wrote.

Mr Adepoju raised questions about whether government can drive reforms in Nigerian football without breaching FIFA’s rules on interference, and whether there are people with the capacity and willingness to take over the running of the game.

He argued that meaningful reform would require the Federal Government and state governors to show genuine interest in football, remove the game from day-to-day politics and support capable people to lead the state football associations, NFF and clubs.

But he also acknowledged the difficult political reality of football administration.

“Who are the people with capacity that deserves to lead the football ecosystem? Do we have options better than what we have now? Are they interested in playing the football politics?” he asked.

For Mr Adepoju, those questions remain unanswered as the September election draws closer.

“In politics across board, power is not given, power is taken through political strategies,” he concluded.

World.title: 26 Katsina LGAs under bandits attack in 2023 – Deputy Governor
World.content:
Katsina State Deputy Governor Faruk Jobe has said about 26 of the state’s 34 local government areas were experiencing persistent attacks when the Dikko Radda administration assumed office in 2023.

Mr Jobe spoke on Thursday while representing the governor at the Second Quarter 2026 North-west Zonal Conference of State Directors of Security at the State Security Service (SSS) headquarters in Katsina.

The conference, themed “Unite Against Terror,” brought together SSS directors and other security officials from across the North-west to discuss terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other security threats affecting the region, Channels Television reported.

Mr Jobe said the 26 local government areas experienced persistent attacks, but claimed the security situation had since improved significantly.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

‘Propaganda is also a form of war’

Channels Television separately reported that Mr Jobe urged stakeholders to use propaganda to help the war against terror and called on the media to exercise greater responsibility in reporting security matters.

He cited the proliferation of citizen’s journalism and warned against what he described as indiscriminate dissemination of information.

However, the publicly reported remarks did not spell out what such a propaganda strategy would entail, including whether Mr Jobe was advocating counter-messaging against armed groups, correcting exaggerated claims about their operations, or limiting publicity around verified security incidents.

26 LGAs once under attack

Mr Jobe said the administration inherited a significantly worse security situation in 2023.

“When we came on board, we had about 26 local governments that were consistently under attack,” The Guardian quoted him as saying.

He said killings, kidnapping for ransom and related crimes were widespread at the time, but that the situation had “improved tremendously” through a combination of kinetic and non-kinetic measures.

The 26-LGA figure provides a new baseline against which the administration’s claim of improvement can be assessed, although Katsina officials have used different descriptions to classify areas affected by insecurity.

An official Katsina State Government publication in January said that before the 2023 general elections, 19 LGAs were considered frontline areas affected by violent banditry and kidnapping.

The descriptions are not necessarily directly comparable. Mr Jobe on Thursday referred to areas that were “consistently under attack”, while the January publication used the narrower classification of “frontline” LGAs.

More recently, the government has divided the state’s 34 LGAs into three security categories.

Commissioner for Internal Security and Home Affairs Nasiru Mu’azu Danmusa said eight LGAs were classified as frontline, 11 as vulnerable and 15 as crisis-free, according to a statement reported by The Nation on 11 August.

Mr Danmusa said the classification was intended to guide the deployment of security personnel, equipment and other resources according to the threat level in each area.

The publicly reported statement did not, however, provide incident-level data or the thresholds used to determine when an LGA moves from frontline to vulnerable or crisis-free status.

Attacks persist despite claimed gains

The government’s claim of significantly improved security comes amid continuing attacks in parts of the state, including Bakori Local Government Area.

On 3 August, PREMIUM TIMES reported that armed attackers killed one resident, injured at least seven and abducted 32 others in Shuwaki community.

One of the abducted women was later released because she was ill and unable to continue the journey, leaving 31 captives at the time the report was published.

The attack followed raids on several neighbouring communities from late July and came days after a major confrontation between security personnel and armed groups in Guga.

Aminu Magaji, a former chairman of Bakori Local Government Area, in the aftermath of the Shuwaki attack said that repeated livestock theft had deprived some farmers of cattle traditionally used for cultivation, forcing residents to work their farms manually.

On Thursday, Daily Trust reported another attack on Unguwar Aminu community in Kandarawa Ward of Bakori, in which two residents were reportedly killed, four others shot and six abducted.

PREMIUM TIMES has not independently verified the casualty and abduction figures in the Unguwar Aminu attack.

Kinetic and non-kinetic measures

Mr Jobe attributed the government’s claimed security gains to collaboration with conventional security agencies, community-based security arrangements and non-kinetic interventions.

He said the government had provided free medical care to victims of bandit attacks and invested in agriculture, mechanisation, improved seeds, fertiliser and agricultural extension services.

He said the administration had recruited and trained 772 agricultural extension workers and equipped them to assist farmers.

The figure is consistent with Mr Radda’s 2025 budget presentation in November 2024, when he said the number of extension workers had increased from 78 in 2023 to 772.

The same budget presentation separately recorded the purchase of 722 motorcycle knapsack sprayers for 722 extension workers.

SSS promises communiqué

Katsina State Director of the SSS Alhassan Iliasu said the conference would enable intelligence agencies across the North-west to review security challenges and develop coordinated counter-terrorism strategies.

He said deliberations at the meeting would culminate in a communiqué that would provide a roadmap for security agencies combating banditry, kidnapping and related crimes across the region, Channels Television reported.

The Chairman of the North-west Forum of State Directors of Security, Hussaini Abubakar, also said the conference was intended to strengthen cooperation and allow security chiefs to exchange experiences.

The Commander of the Nigerian Army’s 17 Brigade in Katsina, Ishaya Ibrahim, stressed the importance of actionable intelligence, intelligence sharing and operational coordination, according to Vanguard.

Katsina State Commissioner of Police Aliyu Fage, similarly said the police and SSS routinely exchanged intelligence and security information to improve their response to threats.

World.title: ANALYSIS: Osun’s 1.9 million voters and the LGAs that may decide the election
World.content:
Osun has 2,339,233 registered voters, out of which 1,906,3,90, who collected the Permanent Voters Card (PVC) are eligible to vote in Saturday’s governorship election.

But the size of the register alone does not show where the election could be decided.

The more revealing question is where those voters are concentrated, how many are likely to turn up and what margins the candidates can build in those areas.

INEC’s figures show that Osogbo has the largest electorate in the state, with 167,704 registered voters, representing 7.17 per cent of the total register.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ife East follows with 128,515 voters, or 5.50 per cent, while Olorunda has 123,063, representing 5.26 per cent. Ife Central has another 122,454 voters, or 5.24 per cent.

Iwo has 106,813 registered voters, representing 4.57 per cent of the state’s electorate. Irewole has 96,528 (4.13 per cent), while Ifelodun has 94,870 (4.06 per cent).

10 LGAs with the largest voter populations account for 1,113,813 registered voters, or 47.6 per cent of the entire register.

That means nearly half of Osun’s registered voters are concentrated in just 10 of the state’s 30 LGAs.

A large register is only potential electoral strength. PVC collection, mobilisation, turnout and the margin each candidate secures will determine how much of that potential becomes actual votes.

INEC said the number of registered voters in Osun rose from 1,954,800 to 2,339,233, an increase of 384,433 voters. But the commission noted that 322,822 newly registered voters had collected their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), representing 62 per cent, before it extended the collection deadline to 31 July.

The figures provide an important qualification to the size of the electorate. A large number of registered voters can give an LGA considerable electoral weight. Still, that weight ultimately depends on how many voters turn up on election day.

The 2022 election provides some useful background, but Saturday’s contest is a different political race.

Ademola Adeleke won the 2022 governorship election with a margin of 28,344 votes against the then incumbent, Gboyega Oyetola of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

This time, Mr Adeleke is seeking another term; the APC is fielding Bola Oyebamiji, while Najeem Salaam is contesting on the platform of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). There are 11 other candidates on the ballot.

So, how is the current distribution of voters likely to shape the 2026 contest?

Ede: a sizeable voting bloc

Ede North has 96,644 registered voters, while Ede South has 67,729.

Together, the two LGAs have 164,373 registered voters, about seven per cent of Osun’s electorate.

That makes Ede one of the state’s important voting blocs.

For Mr Adeleke, the area he hails from carries particular political significance. But the size of the electorate also gives the APC and ADC an incentive to compete for votes there.

What matters on Saturday will be the turnout and the margin each candidate can secure.

Osogbo and Olorunda: more than 290,000 voters

Osogbo has the largest number of registered voters in the state — 167,704, or 7.17 per cent of the total.

Olorunda has another 123,063, representing 5.26 per cent.

Together, the two LGAs in the state capital have 290,767 registered voters, or 12.4 per cent of Osun’s entire register.

That gives the state capital one of the largest concentrations of voters in the election.

The decisive figure could be the eventual margin between the leading candidates after votes are counted.

If turnout is high and the race is closely contested, even a few thousand votes gained or lost in these two LGAs could affect the statewide calculation.

Ife: more than 317,000 registered voters

The three Ife LGAs — Ife East, Ife Central and Ife South — have a combined 317,224 registered voters, about 13.6 per cent of the state’s electorate.

Ife East has 128,515 voters, Ife Central 122,454 and Ife South 66,255.

That makes the Ife axis one of the largest voter concentrations in Osun.

A strong voter turnout could give Ife a great influence on the final result.

Iwo: 106,813 registered voters

Iwo has 106,813 registered voters, representing 4.57 per cent of the state’s electorate.

It is the fifth-largest LGA by voter population.

Ijesa axis: 332,473 voters

The Ijesa axis also commands a substantial voting population.

Ilesa East has 89,491 registered voters, Ilesa West 86,699, Atakumosa East 47,767, Atakumosa West 44,076 and Obokun 64,440.

Together, the five LGAs have 332,473 registered voters, representing about 14.2 per cent of Osun’s entire register.

That is a large enough voting bloc for the candidates to pay close attention to the area.

The medium-sized LGAs matter too

The election will not be decided only in the biggest voter centres.

Irewole has 96,528 registered voters, Ifelodun 94,870 and Ejigbo 87,676.

Oriade has 84,283, Odo-Otin 82,574, Boripe 81,067 and Ayedaade 77,649.

Other sizeable electorates include Egbedore with 67,440, Irepodun with 67,131, Ife North with 65,718, Isokan with 65,379 and Obokun with 64,440.

Even the smaller LGAs contribute to the final arithmetic: Orolu has 51,021 registered voters, Atakumosa West 44,076, Ola-Oluwa 44,761 and Boluwaduro 29,797, while Ifedayo has 28,361.

But taken together, the votes from the state’s medium and smaller LGAs could provide the difference in a closely fought election.

Three candidates, different arithmetic

The presence of three major candidates also makes the calculation less straightforward.

Governor Adeleke, Mr Oyebamiji and Mr Salaam do not need to win every large LGA to remain competitive.

What matters is the combination of votes and margins.

A candidate could lose a large LGA narrowly and remain competitive, while a heavy defeat in another area could create a gap that becomes difficult to recover elsewhere.

The ADC’s performance could also influence the race even without winning a large number of LGAs.

If Mr Salaam attracts substantial support in areas where Mr Adeleke and Mr Oyebamiji are closely matched, his votes could alter the margin between the two leading candidates.

That makes the distribution of votes more important than simply the statewide total.

The register is only the starting point

Some registered voters may not vote. Others may have registered in places where they no longer live. The number who actually turn up, and where they turn up, could therefore change the weight of the figures considerably.

There is also a constitutional requirement beyond securing the highest number of votes.

A governorship candidate must obtain the highest number of votes and at least one-quarter of the votes cast in at least two-thirds of the LGAs.

With 30 LGAs in Osun, that means meeting the one-quarter threshold in at least 20 LGAs.

So the candidates cannot concentrate entirely on the state’s biggest voter centres.

They need both numbers and geographical spread.

That is the central calculation behind Saturday’s election.

Osogbo’s 167,704 voters matter. So do Ife East’s 128,515, Olorunda’s 123,063, Ife Central’s 122,454 and Iwo’s 106,813.

But the smaller LGAs matter too.

The winner will ultimately be the candidate who can turn support across enough of those areas into actual votes — and build a statewide margin large enough to finish ahead.

What the experts say

Development consultant and public affairs analyst Jide Ojo said the increase in Osun’s voter register was not surprising, given the registration exercises conducted since the last governorship election.

But he noted that the distribution of voters across the state deserved more attention.

Mr Ojo identified Ede North and Ede South as particularly important to Adeleke because of his strong performance there in 2022.

He also pointed to Osogbo, Olorunda, the three Ife LGAs, Atakumosa East and West, Obokun and the wider Ijesa axis.

He does not expect a landslide.

“I don’t expect that any of the candidates, whoever will win, will have a landslide victory,” he said, predicting that the final margin could be between 20,000 and 30,000 votes or even less.

If that prediction is close to the final result, relatively small changes in the larger LGAs could determine the winner.

Legal practitioner and public affairs analyst Liborous Oshoma told PREMIUM TIMES that candidates must also look beyond the biggest voter centres because of the constitutional requirement for geographical spread.

“You must concentrate on having a spread, and then you begin to look at where the population is, where you would get more numbers to add to your numbers,” Mr Oshoma said.

Ezenwa Nwagwu, co-convener of the Say No Campaign and Executive Director of the Peering Advocacy and Advancement Centre in Africa (PAACA), cautioned against using the voter register as a substitute for turnout.

“There is voter apathy. There is voter turnout. They don’t mean the same thing,” he said.

Mr Nwagwu said people could register and still stay away because of fear, intimidation, their perception of government or the influence of money in elections.

He also pointed to students and other residents who may be registered in an area but be elsewhere on election day.

He urged political parties, security agencies and INEC to ensure that voters can participate freely.

“The executive agencies must be professional and impartial. INEC must follow its own regulations and ensure that everyone is given the opportunity to cast their votes without let or hindrance,” he stated.

World.title: Two arraigned for alleged gang-rape of 13-year-old girl lured with chicken
World.content:
The police have arraigned two men before a senior magistrate’s court in Minna for allegedly gang-raping a 13-year-old girl.

The defendants, Awal Bala, 40, and Danjuma Ibrahim, 43, popularly known as DJ, face a two-count charge of receiving stolen property and unlawful sexual intercourse with a child.

The prosecution alleged that the defendants, who reside at the same address, lured the teenager into their residence with a stolen chicken before allegedly having sexual intercourse with her several times.

Prosecuting counsel, Zubairu Wuna, told the court that police investigations established that the two men allegedly used the stolen chicken to entice the girl into their house, where the alleged sexual assault took place.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to the prosecution, the offences are punishable under Section 316 of the Niger State Penal Code Law 2025 and Section 26(2) of the Niger State Child Rights and Protection Law 2021, as amended.

When the charges were read to them before Senior Magistrate Ummi Imam, both defendants pleaded not guilty.

Defence counsel, Jerry Ekeh, subsequently made an oral application for their bail, arguing that his clients were presumed innocent until proven guilty by the court.

The prosecution, however, opposed the application, arguing that one of the offences was capital in nature.

In her ruling, the magistrate, Mrs Imam, refused the bail application, stressing that the grant of bail remained at the discretion of the court.

“In view of the capital nature of one of the charges against the defendants, the bail application is hereby refused,” the magistrate ruled.

The court consequently ordered that the defendants be remanded in correctional custody and adjourned the case until 19 August for definite hearing.

Background: Another gang-rape of a 13-year-old

The case comes barely two months after a senior magistrate’s court in Minna sentenced four men to a combined 95 years in prison for gang-raping and impregnating a 13-year-old girl in Kontagora, Niger State.

The convicts — Salisu Baura, Lawali Sha’ibu, Haruna Sa’idu and Bello — were convicted of joint act and unlawful sexual intercourse with a child. The court described their conduct as “animalistic, inhuman, and heartless.”

The girl was reportedly subjected to sexual abuse by the men in 2023, resulting in her pregnancy.

The suspects were arrested by operatives of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps in Kontagora.

In another reported incident, PREMIUM TIMES reported in November 2025 that three suspected terrorists allegedly raped a 13-year-old girl in Kudodo community, Shiroro Local Government Area, Niger State.

The girl was reportedly returning from Galadima Kogo market when the incident occurred and was subsequently hospitalised.

The recurring cases have continued to raise concerns about the protection of children and the need for stronger enforcement of child-protection laws in Niger State.

World.title: Police arrest 29-yr-old man for desecrating Qur’an for ritual in Zuru
World.content:
File image.

By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi

The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested one Abubakar Musa, male, 29, of Rafin Mose Village, Zuru LGA, in connection with a case of criminal conspiracy, abuse of religious books, use of spells and hypnosis, and inciting disturbance.

Kebbi Police Command spokesperson, SP Bashir Usman, in a statement on Friday, said the incident occurred on 9th August 2026 at about 1900hrs in the Zango Area, Zuru.

According to him, preliminary investigation revealed that the suspect allegedly conspired with two others; Rabi’u Tela, husband of Zarau Hassan, and Hamza Zango, both now at large, to dig a pit inside Zarau Hassan’s room and bury therein a copy of the Holy Qur’an, together with semen, white and red kolanuts, underwear, dead animals, and other fetish items.

The act was allegedly intended to make Zarau Hassan more submissive to her husband, Rabi’u Tela, and was carried out in circumstances capable of provoking a breach of the peace among the Muslim faithful in the community.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Umar M. Hadejia, strongly condemns the alleged act and warns that the Command will deal decisively, within the law, with individuals whose actions threaten religious harmony, public order, and peaceful coexistence.

World.title: Hudspeth takes over as US Consul General in Lagos
World.content:
By Vera Anyagafu

The United States Consulate General in Lagos has announced the arrival of its new Consul General, Mr. Brandon Hudspeth, who officially begins a three-year tour as the senior US government representative across states in Nigeria.

Mr. Hudspeth, a career member of the Senior Foreign Service, takes over from Consul General Rick Swart, who retired from the US Foreign Service in July 2026.

The appointment marks Hudspeth’s second posting to Lagos, after he previously served as Political-Economic Section Chief at the Consulate from 2020 to 2022, a period that deepened US engagement in trade, governance, and regional security.

‘HONORED TO RETURN’

Making his first statement from Lagos, Consul General Hudspeth said he was excited to be back to serve in Nigeria.

According to him, “I am honored to return to Lagos as the US Consul General. I know firsthand the strength of the US-Nigeria partnership and the extraordinary energy, ingenuity, and entrepreneurial spirit that Nigerians and Americans share.”

He said his priorities during his tenure will include reconnecting with long-standing partners, building new relationships, and working with Nigerian stakeholders to expand bilateral trade and investment.

“I look forward to working alongside Nigerians to drive innovation, strengthen collaboration in the technology and creative industries, and create new opportunities that advance shared prosperity for both countries,” he also said.

TWO DECADES DIPLOMATIC EXPERIENCE

Consul General Hudspeth brings more than 20 years of diplomatic experience across Africa, Asia, Latin America, and Washington, D.C.

Most recently, he served as Deputy Chief of Mission at the US Embassy in Windhoek, Namibia.

Prior to that, he was Director of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement at the US Embassy in Manila, Philippines, where he oversaw US civilian assistance programs in law enforcement, rule of law, counter-narcotics, and maritime security cooperation.

His other overseas assignments include Political-Economic Section Chief in Bamako, Mali; Nonimmigrant Visa Chief in Havana, Cuba; and Political-Military Officer in Kabul, Afghanistan.

In Washington, he served in the Department of State’s Operations Center, on the Secretariat Staff supporting the Secretary of State, and as a Desk Officer in the Bureau of African Affairs.

ACADEMIC BACKGROUND

A native of Texas, Consul General Hudspeth is a Phi Beta Kappa graduate of Morehouse College, where he earned a Bachelor’s degree in Political Science and Economics.

He holds a Master of Public Policy from Harvard University’s Kennedy School and is also a Distinguished Graduate of the National Defense University, where he obtained a Master of Science in National Resource Strategy.

The US Consulate General in Lagos covers 17 states in southern Nigeria and plays a central role in advancing US interests in the region, including commercial ties, consular services, educational exchange, and cooperation in health, security, and culture.

With Nigeria remaining one of the United States’ key partners in Africa, officials say Hudspeth’s return to Lagos comes at a pivotal time as both countries seek to deepen economic collaboration and people-to-people ties.

World.title: Arsenal plot sensational Victor Osimhen move after Vinicius Jr snub
World.content:
Arsenal are reportedly considering a sensational late move for Nigerian striker Victor Osimhen as they continue to explore attacking options before the transfer window closes.

The Gunners have endured a difficult summer in their pursuit of attacking reinforcements, having missed out on Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr, while potential moves for Julian Alvarez and Bradley Barcola are also appearing increasingly difficult to complete.

Osimhen, who currently plays for Galatasaray, has emerged as a potential alternative as Arsenal look to strengthen their forward line.

The Nigeria international enjoyed a prolific spell in Turkey last season and remains one of Europe’s most sought-after strikers.

Arsenal are also working on defensive reinforcements and reportedly want to sign Aston Villa and England defender Ezri Konsa before the deadline.

Meanwhile, Manchester United’s main priority remains the signing of a new left-back, although Newcastle are reluctant to sell their key target, Lewis Hall. Michael Carrick’s side could also look to strengthen in midfield and attack.

Liverpool, meanwhile, are continuing negotiations for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola. However, the Reds are reportedly unwilling to meet PSG’s £145 million asking price.

The Premier League clubs are therefore expected to remain active in the final stages of the transfer window as they seek to complete their respective squads.

World.title: Tinubu calls for peaceful election in Osun, charges security agencies to protect voters, INEC officials
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission and the security agencies to ensure a peaceful and transparent election in Osun State.

The people of Osun State will go to the polls on Saturday, August 15, 2026, to elect their governor in an election where 15 candidates are contesting.

Among them are the incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke, the All Progressives Congress, APC, candidate, Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji, and the African Democratic Congress, ADC candidate, Hon. Najeem Salaam.

President Tinubu also charged the electorate in Osun State to come out to discharge their civic responsibility and eschew any act that could disrupt the peaceful conduct of the election, while assuring the people of their safety before and after the polls.

“As the people of Osun State head to the polling units to elect who will govern them in the next four years, I call on the Independent National Electoral Commission to ensure orderly conduct of the election.

“The election must be transparent, free and fair. I urge INEC to ensure the integrity of the process,” the President said.

“INEC must use this last off-cycle election as a test case to demonstrate to Nigerians their full preparedness for the 2027 polls,” he added.

“I have charged the Inspector-General of Police and other heads of security outfits taking part in the election to provide maximum security at polling units. No room should be allowed for troublemakers to disrupt the process.

“Electoral officials and voters must be protected so they can perform their civic duties without fear or intimidation.

“Voters should feel confident to go out in their numbers to vote for the candidate of their choice as all measures necessary to ensure a peaceful, free and fair election have been put in place.

“Our elections must be credible, and the outcome of the Osun Governorship election must reflect the will of the people,” Tinubu declared.

World.title: Tiv, Arewa youths laud Tinubu over creation of Army Division in Benue
World.content:
..hold joint peaceful rally

By Peter Duru, Makurdi

The Tiv Youth Council, TYC, Worldwide and the Arewa Youth Assembly, AYA, have commended President Bola Tinubu for approving the creation of the 5 Division of the Nigerian Army, with headquarters in Makurdi, Benue State, describing the development as a major boost to security in the North Central region.

The youth groups gave the commendation on Friday, during a joint peaceful rally organised in Makurdi to appreciate President Tinubu, the Chief of Defence Staff, Gen. Olufemi Oluyede, and the Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Waidi Shaibu, for the establishment of the new Army division.

In an address delivered on behalf of the TYC Worldwide, its Secretary, Emmanuel Katseen, said the creation of the division was a significant response to years of security challenges confronting Benue communities.

Katseen said the state had endured armed attacks, kidnappings, banditry, militia activities and communal conflicts, resulting in loss of lives, destruction of property, displacement of residents and disruption of agricultural activities.

According to him, “for decades, Benue State has faced serious security challenges, including armed attacks, kidnappings, banditry, militia activities and communal conflicts. These have led to loss of lives, destruction of property, displacement and disruption of farming activities, threatening our status as the Food Basket of the Nation.”

He said the TYC had consistently advocated stronger security measures to protect communities and enable displaced residents to return to their homes and farms, describing President Tinubu’s approval of the 5 Division as evidence of his administration’s commitment to the security and welfare of Nigerians, while also commending the military leadership for strengthening security operations in the region.

He said the new division would strengthen military command and control in Benue and the North Central, improve rapid response to security threats, protect farming communities and facilitate the restoration of agricultural activities.

The Tiv youth leader also expressed optimism that the division would create opportunities for youth recruitment and empowerment in the Nigerian Army, while stimulating socio-economic development through improved infrastructure and increased economic activities.

The council pledged its cooperation with the new division and other security agencies, promising to support credible intelligence sharing, mobilise youths to embrace peace and discourage the harbouring or protection of criminals.

It also called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, community leaders, youth organisations and residents across Benue and the North Central region to support the military and other security agencies in their efforts to restore lasting peace.

Similarly, the Publicity Secretary of the Arewa Youth Assembly, Aliyu Muhammad, described the creation of the 5 Division as a historic development and a demonstration of political will by the Tinubu administration.

Muhammad, who spoke at the rally, said the expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions and the establishment of the 5 Division in Benue represented a major elevation of the state’s strategic importance in the country’s security architecture.

“Today is not a day for long grammar, but for loud gratitude, for the expansion of the Nigerian Army, from eight to 12 divisions and the establishment of the 5th Division in Benue State by President Tinubu,” he said.

According to him, Benue had historically hosted Army brigades but had now been elevated to the status of a full division headquarters, describing the development as evidence that the President was committed to fulfilling his campaign promises, particularly on security.

Muhammad said the strategic location of the division would enable it to respond not only to security threats in Benue but also to challenges in neighbouring Nasarawa and Kogi states, as well as other parts of the North Central.

While urging the Federal Government to provide adequate funding and modern military equipment to enable the new division to discharge its responsibilities effectively, he said, “we must also add our voices to call on the President to ensure adequate funding for this new Division and the provision of modern equipment to aid its work.

The Arewa youth leader, who expressed confidence that the presence of the new division would contribute significantly to tackling insecurity in the region and restoring public confidence, also commended the Chief of Defence Staff and Chief of Army Staff for their leadership, courage, experience and expertise in military operations, saying their efforts had placed the country on a path of renewed confidence.

Muhammad further charged the General Officer Commanding the new 5 Division to maintain close engagement with the people of Benue, particularly the youths, and ensure that the host community remained an important partner in the division’s operation. “Carry the people of Benue along as your host community, especially the youths, and act always in their best interest,” he added.

World.title: Adeleke camp condemns release of APC Assembly candidate allegedly found with gun
World.content:
Osun governor, Ademola Adeleke

The Imole Campaign Council has commended the Nigerian Navy for what it described as professionalism and neutrality in Osun State, while condemning the reported release of an All Progressives Congress House of Assembly candidate allegedly arrested with a gun.

In a statement issued on Friday by its spokesman, Pelumi Olajengbesi, the council said its attention had been drawn to “the arrest and subsequent controversial release of an All Progressives Congress member, Babatunde Festus Komolafe, who is also the APC House of Assembly candidate for Atakumosa East/West Local Government Area.”

According to the statement, Komolafe, popularly known as BFK, was apprehended by naval personnel in his hometown of Ifewara on Thursday.

The council alleged that “during a routine search conducted by men of the Nigerian Navy, the APC candidate was arrested alongside his supporters while travelling in a campaign vehicle reportedly belonging to the APC after a gun was allegedly discovered in the vehicle.”

It said the arrest had become public knowledge after a video of the suspects circulated widely on social media.

“The arrest is no secret, as a video showing the suspects has since gone viral and attracted public outrage,” the statement read.

The campaign council further claimed that the suspects were released shortly after their arrest due to pressure from senior APC figures.

“However, we gathered reliably that the arrested APC candidate and his co-perpetrators were immediately released following pressure from APC top goons,” it stated.

The statement added that “a news outlet even chronicled how the naval officer in charge was forced to release the suspects and asked to step aside.”

Despite its criticism of the release, the council praised the conduct of the armed forces during the ongoing governorship election campaigns.

“The Imole Campaign Council commends the men and officers of the Nigerian Armed Forces, especially the Nigerian Navy, for their neutrality and professionalism since the commencement of the governorship election campaigns,” the statement said.

It added, “The men and officers of the Nigerian Armed Forces have been proactive in arresting troublemakers regardless of party affiliation. Special salute to our gallant troops!”

The council, however, insisted that releasing a suspect allegedly found with an unauthorised firearm was dangerous.

“That said, the release of a suspect who was caught with an unauthorised gun is unacceptable. It sends the wrong signal to political criminals whose pastime is killing and maiming,” the statement declared.

The group linked the incident to what it described as the APC’s past conduct in Osun State.

“This is particularly alarming because of the APC’s antecedents in Osun. Just two weeks ago, the police launched an attack on military personnel to rescue five APC hoodlums, including the notorious APC thug, Asiri Eniba, arrested by the Nigerian Navy for shooting sporadically in Ile-Ife with pump-action guns,” it alleged.

The council called on the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, to intervene.

“We call on the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, to look into this grave injustice and punish the suspects,” the statement said.

It concluded, “No politician is above the law, and no political thug should be released to keep fomenting trouble.”

World.title: SEC blacklists 6 individuals, 3 entities for financing terrorism
World.content:
By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has directed capital market operators to freeze the funds, assets and other economic resources belonging to six individuals and three entities designated as terrorist financiers by the Nigeria Sanctions Committee (NSC).

The SEC, in a circular to all Capital Market Regulated Entities (CMREs) on Friday said the designations were made in line with the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act (TPPA) 2022.

The six individuals are Babangida Muhammed Adamu Hammajam, Abdullahi Umar Usman, Ibrahim Abubakar, Adamu Chiroma, Muktar Muhammad Adamu and Yakubu Ogirima Ibrahim.

The three designated entities are Nine to Nine BDC Ltd, Generation Currency BDC Ltd and Abbal Bako & Sons Bureau de Change.

According to the SEC, Hammajama was listed on June 18, 2026, for involvement in terrorism financing and support for the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), while Usman was designated for providing material support to a designated terrorist organisation through repeated financial transactions.

The commission said Abubakar was listed for involvement in terrorism financing and membership of ISWAP, while Chiroma was designated for allegedly using Bureau De Change (BDC) operations and related corporate entities to facilitate the movement of funds linked to terrorist activities.

Muktar Muhammad Adamu was listed on June 15, 2026, for providing financial support and facilitating transactions linked to the financing network of the ISWAP Okene cell, while Ibrahim was designated for providing material and financial support to the ISWAP Kogi cell.

The SEC said the three entities were listed for their alleged involvement in facilitating and channelling funds connected to the ISWAP Okene financing network.

The commission directed CMREs to immediately identify and freeze, without prior notice, all funds, assets and other economic resources in their possession belonging to the designated persons and entities.

They are also required to report frozen assets and other compliance actions, including attempted transactions, to the Secretariat of the Nigeria Sanctions Committee.

In addition, the SEC directed regulated entities to immediately file suspicious transaction reports with the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) for further analysis of the financial activities.

It further instructed operators to report all cases of name matches in financial transactions as suspicious, whether occurring before or after receipt of the sanctions list.

The regulated entities are also required to prohibit dealings with the designated persons and entities and continue monitoring for transactions involving them.

The SEC said any findings should be reported to the Nigeria Sanctions Committee through its designated reporting channel.

The circular takes immediate effect, with the commission warning that failure to comply would constitute a violation of the Investments and Securities Act, 2025, and the SEC Anti-Money Laundering/Combating the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) Rules and Regulations.

It said violations could attract regulatory sanctions, including fines, suspension of operations or revocation of registration.

The SEC further reminded capital market operators that all unusual or suspicious transactions must be promptly reported to the NFIU.
